title.zh: 卷四百〇四 列傳第一百六十三 汪若海 張運 柳約 李舜臣 孫逢吉 章穎 商飛卿 劉穎 徐邦憲
title.en: Volume 404 Biographies 163: Wang Ruohai, Zhang Yun, Liu Yue, Li Shunchen, Sun Fengji, Zhang Ying, Shang Feiqing, Liu Ying, Xu Bangxian
title.raw: 卷四百〇四 列傳第一百六十三 汪若海 張運 柳約 李舜臣 孫逢吉 章穎 商飛卿 劉穎 徐邦憲 Volume 404 Biographies 163: Wang Ruohai, Zhang Yun, Liu Yue, Li Shunchen, Sun Fengji, Zhang Ying, Shang Feiqing, Liu Ying, Xu Bangxian

sentences.zh: 汪若海

translations.literal: Wang Ruohai
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruohai

sentences.zh: 京城失守，若海述麟為書以獻。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Ruohai composed the Book of Lin as a memorial and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was lost, Ruohai wrote up the Book of Lin and submitted it as a memorial.

sentences.zh: 及二帝北行，袖書抗粘罕，請存趙氏。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were taken north, he concealed a letter and presented it to Nianhan, pleading to preserve the house of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors were marched north as captives, he hid a letter on his person and presented it to Nianhan, begging that the Zhao house be spared.

sentences.zh: 縋而出，謁康王於濟州，謂神器久虛，異姓僭竊，宜蚤即位，以圖中興。

translations.literal: He was let down by rope and escaped, then went to pay respects to Prince Kang at Jizhou, saying the sacred vessel had long stood empty while men of another surname usurped it unjustly—that he ought to take the throne early to plan restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He was lowered over the wall by rope and made his escape, then went to see Prince Kang at Jizhou. He told the prince that the imperial regalia had long stood vacant while outsiders seized power in usurpation, and that he ought to ascend the throne without delay to plan the restoration of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 一日間三被顧問，補修職郎，充帳前差使。

translations.literal: Within a single day he was consulted three times, was given the post of Xiuzhi Lang, and served as an attendant in the prince's tent.
translations.idiomatic: In the space of a single day he was summoned for counsel three times, was appointed Xiuzhi Lang, and served as an attendant in the prince's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 高宗既即位，推恩改承奉郎，遷江南經制使，轉承事郎，監登聞檢院。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozong had taken the throne, by grace of promotion he was made Chengfeng Lang, transferred to Jiangnan Jingzhi Commissioner, then Chenshi Lang, and supervised the Dengwen Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Gaozong had ascended the throne, Ruohai received a favoring promotion to Chengfeng Lang, was made commissioner for the Jiangnan circuit, advanced to Chenshi Lang, and served as superintendent of the Dengwen Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 五府交辟，改屬右府。

translations.literal: The Five Offices all invited him in succession, and he was reassigned to the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: All five military offices sought him out in turn, and he was transferred to serve under the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以張浚宣撫川、陝，議未決。

translations.literal: The court proposed Zhang Jun as pacification commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi, but the matter was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The court was considering appointing Zhang Jun pacification commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi, but the decision had not yet been made.

sentences.zh: 若海曰：「天下者，常山蛇勢也，秦、蜀為首，東南為尾，中原為脊。

translations.literal: Ruohai said: "All under Heaven is like the posture of the Mount Chang serpent: Qin and Shu are the head, the southeast the tail, and the Central Plain the spine.
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai said, "The realm is like the Mount Chang serpent of stratagem: Qin and Shu form the head, the southeast the tail, and the Central Plain the spine.

sentences.zh: 今以東南為首，安能起天下之脊哉？

translations.literal: Now to take the southeast as the head—how can one raise the spine of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If we take the southeast as our head now, how can we ever raise up the spine of the realm?

sentences.zh: 將圖恢復，必在川、陝。

translations.literal: If one wishes to plan recovery, it must lie in Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Any plan for recovery must center on Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 」乃往見浚，極談終日，浚大驚，辟以自隨，以親老辭。

translations.literal: " He then went to see Jun and talked with him at length all day; Jun was greatly astonished and invited him to accompany him, but Ruohai declined on the grounds that his parents were elderly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went to see Zhang Jun and talked with him the whole day through. Jun was deeply impressed and invited him to join his staff, but Ruohai declined because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 繼論軍食，迕執政，通判沅州，以讒奪籍，謫英州。

translations.literal: He later discussed army provisions, ran afoul of the chief ministers, was made vice-prefect of Yuanzhou, was stripped of his registry entry on account of slander, and was banished to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he spoke out on army provisions, he offended the chief ministers. He was made vice-prefect of Yuanzhou, then stripped of his official standing on a charge of slander and exiled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 道出臨川，時節制江夏軍馬李允文擁眾數十萬，跋扈不用朝命，朝廷命招討使張俊屯江西，參謀官湯東野與若海故，得若海道中，喜甚。

translations.literal: Passing through Linchuan on the road, at that time Li Yunwen, who controlled the Jiangxia army and horses and held several hundred thousand men, was overbearing and would not obey court orders. The court ordered Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun to encamp in Jiangxi. Staff officer Tang Dongye was an old acquaintance of Ruohai's; he met Ruohai on the road and was exceedingly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On his journey he passed through Linchuan. At that time Li Yunwen, commander of the Jiangxia forces, held several hundred thousand troops and defied the court with arrogant insubordination. The court ordered Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun to encamp in Jiangxi. Staff officer Tang Dongye, an old friend of Ruohai's, met him along the road and was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「李允文懷反側，非君莫能開其自新。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Li Yunwen harbors rebellious intent; no one but you can open the way for him to reform.
translations.idiomatic: He told Ruohai, "Li Yunwen is nursing treacherous designs. No one but you can persuade him to return to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」若海即馳往，諭以成敗逆順，示以朝廷威德，復談三策以動之，辭旨明暢。

translations.literal: " Ruohai immediately rode there, instructed him on success and failure and on what accords with or defies the times, displayed the court's majesty and virtue, and again set forth three stratagems to move him; his words were clear and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruohai rode to him at once. He explained the logic of success and failure and of loyalty versus rebellion, set forth the court's authority and benevolence, and laid out three stratagems to sway him, speaking with lucid force.

sentences.zh: 允文大感悟，即舉軍東下。

translations.literal: Yunwen was deeply moved to understanding and immediately led his army east.
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen was deeply stirred and at once marched his army east in submission.

sentences.zh: 若海復為書招其徒張用、曹成、李宏、馬友同歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Ruohai again wrote letters to summon his followers Zhang Yong, Cao Cheng, Li Hong, and Ma You to return together to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai also wrote letters calling on his followers Zhang Yong, Cao Cheng, Li Hong, and Ma You to submit together to the court.

sentences.zh: 用一見，以其眾二十萬解甲效順，惟成疑貳有他志，若海移書責之。

translations.literal: Yong, on a single meeting, with his two hundred thousand men laid down arms and submitted; only Cheng was of two minds and had other designs, and Ruohai sent a letter rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting Yong disarmed his two hundred thousand men and submitted. Only Cheng wavered with other designs in mind, and Ruohai sent him a reproachful letter.

sentences.zh: 成怒，將殺若海，若海夜宿王林軍帳，以計得林軍印，遂奪其眾五千人。

translations.literal: Cheng was enraged and was about to kill Ruohai. Ruohai lodged overnight in Wang Lin's army tent, and by stratagem obtained Lin's army seal, then seized his force of five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng flew into a rage and was about to kill Ruohai. Ruohai spent the night in Wang Lin's camp, contrived to obtain Lin's army seal, and thereby took command of his five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 翼日，成遂遁。

translations.literal: The next day Cheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: The following day Cheng fled.

sentences.zh: 若海遺宏書，使刺成以自歸；

translations.literal: Ruohai sent Hong a letter, having him assassinate Cheng to win his own return;
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai sent Hong a letter instructing him to kill Cheng and thereby earn his own pardon;

sentences.zh: 宏得書圖成而力不勝，復走長沙刺友，群盜解散。

translations.literal: Hong received the letter and plotted against Cheng but lacked the strength to prevail; he again went to Changsha to assassinate You, and the bandit hosts dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong received the letter and plotted against Cheng but could not overcome him. He then went to Changsha to kill Ma You, and the bandit bands broke up and scattered.

sentences.zh: 若海遂以林五千人歸招討使張俊，俊乃班師凱旋，軍容愈盛。

translations.literal: Ruohai then returned Lin's five thousand men to Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun; Jun thereupon withdrew his army in triumph, and his military presence grew ever more imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai then brought Wang Lin's five thousand troops back to Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun. Jun withdrew his army in triumph, and his forces appeared more formidable than ever.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方出師，若海以為為國家者，當化盜賊為我用，不可失英雄為國患。

translations.literal: At that time the court was just dispatching troops on campaign. Ruohai held that those who serve the state ought to turn bandits to our use and must not lose heroes only to make them a peril to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then launching campaigns, and Ruohai argued that a state ought to turn bandits into instruments of its power and must not let heroes slip away to become national dangers.

sentences.zh: 因獻平寇策，朝廷悉用之。

translations.literal: He thereupon presented a strategy for pacifying bandits, and the court adopted it in full.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan for pacifying the bandits, and the court adopted it entirely.

sentences.zh: 其後李宏為劉忠所並，死長沙；

translations.literal: Afterward Li Hong was absorbed by Liu Zhong and died at Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Hong was absorbed by Liu Zhong and died at Changsha;

sentences.zh: 劉忠為韓世忠所破，走劉豫；

translations.literal: Liu Zhong was defeated by Han Shizhong and fled to Liu Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong was broken by Han Shizhong and fled to Liu Yu;

sentences.zh: 曹成走廣而復降，湖湘遂安。

translations.literal: Cao Cheng fled to Guang and then submitted again, and the lakes and Xiang region were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng fled into Guang and later surrendered again, and the Hunan region was finally brought to peace.

sentences.zh: 尋復承務郎、監潭州南岳廟、通判辰州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored to Chengwu Lang, made superintendent of the Nanyue Temple in Tanzhou, and made vice-prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to Chengwu Lang, appointed superintendent of the Nanyue Temple at Tanzhou, and made vice-prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，復三京，祗謁陵寢，事還，以前功，旬月四遷至承議郎、通判順昌府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, when the three capitals were recovered, he reverently visited the imperial tombs. When the mission returned, on account of his earlier merit, within ten days he was promoted four times to Chengji Lang and vice-prefect of Shunchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, when the three capitals were recovered, he paid reverent visit to the imperial tombs. On his return, his earlier services won him four promotions within a single month, to Chengji Lang and vice-prefect of Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 金人奄至，太尉劉錡甫至，眾不滿三萬，遣人丐援於朝，無敢往者。

translations.literal: The Jurchens suddenly arrived. Grand Marshal Liu Qi had only just come, and his force numbered fewer than thirty thousand. He sent men to beg aid from the court, but no one dared go.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens swept in unexpectedly. Grand Marshal Liu Qi had only just arrived with fewer than thirty thousand men. He sent envoys begging the court for reinforcements, but no one dared go.

sentences.zh: 若海毅然請行，具述錡明方略，善用兵，以偏師濟之，必有成功，朝廷從之，金兵果敗去。

translations.literal: Ruohai resolutely requested to go, fully setting forth that Qi was clear in strategy and skilled in employing troops—that with a detached column to assist him there would surely be success. The court agreed, and the Jurchen army was indeed defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai boldly volunteered to go. He explained at length that Qi was brilliant in strategy and adept at command, and that a supporting detachment would surely bring success. The court agreed, and the Jurchen forces were indeed driven off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 辟淮北宣撫司主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was invited to serve as director of planning documents in the Huabei Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as director of planning documents for the Huabei Pacification Office.

sentences.zh: 拓皐之役，復以勞兩轉至朝散郎、通判洪州，未上，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Tuogao, he was again promoted twice for merit to Chaosan Lang and vice-prefect of Hongzhou, but before taking up the post he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle at Tuogao he was twice promoted for merit to Chaosan Lang and vice-prefect of Hongzhou, but before he could take up the post he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，添差通判信州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was given an additional assignment as vice-prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he received an additional appointment as vice-prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷湖北帥司參議。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was transferred to staff adviser in the Hubei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he was transferred to staff adviser on the Hubei military commission.

sentences.zh: 知道州，陛辭得對，上曰：「久不見卿，卿向安在？

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Daozhou. At his audience on departing the capital he was granted a response. The emperor said: "It has been long since I have seen you—where have you been?
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Daozhou. At his farewell audience the emperor spoke with him directly. "I have not seen you in a long while," the emperor said. "Where have you been?

sentences.zh: 」授直秘閣、知江州，丁父憂。

translations.literal: " He was given the post of Direct Secretariat Drafter and made prefect of Jiangzhou, then entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Direct Secretariat Drafter and prefect of Jiangzhou, then went into mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 時方經略中原，朝廷議起若海，而若海死矣。

translations.literal: At that time they were just planning operations in the Central Plain, and the court deliberated recalling Ruohai—but Ruohai was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then planning operations to recover the Central Plain and debated recalling Ruohai—but by then Ruohai was already dead.

sentences.zh: 若海豁達高亮，深沈有度，恥為世俗章句學，為文操紙筆立就，蹈厲風發。

translations.literal: Ruohai was open and magnanimous, lofty and bright, deep and measured in bearing. He was ashamed of the conventional study of textual glosses; when he wrote, he took brush and paper and finished at once, vigorous and swift as a rising wind.
translations.idiomatic: Ruohai was magnanimous and high-minded, reserved yet measured in deportment. He disdained the pedantry of conventional textual scholarship. When he wrote, he took up brush and paper and finished on the spot, his prose forceful and swift.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗以片紙書若海名諭張浚曰：「似此人材，卿宜收拾。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once wrote Ruohai's name on a slip of paper and instructed Zhang Jun: "A talent like this—you ought to gather him in.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once wrote Ruohai's name on a slip of paper and told Zhang Jun, "A man of this caliber is one you ought to bring into your service.

sentences.zh: 」會浚去國，不果召。

translations.literal: " But it happened that Jun left the capital, and the summons was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " But Jun left office before the summons could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 張運，字南仲，信之貴溪人，唐宰相文瓘之後。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun, style name Nanzhong, was a native of Guixi in Xin Prefecture and a descendant of the Tang chancellor Zhang Wenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun, courtesy name Nanzhong, was a native of Guixi in Xin Prefecture and a descendant of the Tang chancellor Zhang Wenguan.

sentences.zh: 父貫，右通直郎，累贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Guan was Right Tongzhi Lang and was posthumously ennobled to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guan held the rank of Right Tongzhi Lang and was posthumously ennobled to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 運年二十五，以太學生登宣和三年進士第，賜同上舍出身，調桂陽監藍山縣丞。

translations.literal: At twenty-five Yun, as a student of the Imperial Academy, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Xuanhe, was granted the status of tongshangshe chushen, and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Lanshan County in Guiyang Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five, while a student at the Imperial Academy, Yun passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Xuanhe, received the status of tongshangshe chushen, and was appointed assistant magistrate of Lanshan County under the Guiyang Superintendency.

sentences.zh: 縣闕令，運攝縣事。

translations.literal: The county lacked a magistrate, and Yun acted in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no magistrate, so Yun assumed charge of county affairs.

sentences.zh: 縣與諸獠接壤，因俗為治，吏民安之。

translations.literal: The county bordered the various Liao peoples; he governed according to local custom, and officials and people alike were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered various tribal peoples. He governed according to local custom, and officials and commoners alike lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 臨武寇與諸獠合，大剽掠，運親帥兵禽之。

translations.literal: Bandits from Linwu joined with the various Liao in great plundering raids; Yun personally led troops and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits from Linwu joined the tribal peoples in widespread pillaging. Yun personally led troops and captured them.

sentences.zh: 遷潭州攸縣尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be defender of You County in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of defender of You County in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，劇賊王在據岐山，潭帥徴兵戍岳，運將二千人先至岳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed south, the fierce bandit Wang Zai held Qishan. The Tanzhou commander levied troops to garrison Yue; Yun led two thousand men and arrived at Yue first.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong fled south, the fierce rebel Wang Zai seized Qishan. The Tanzhou commander raised troops to garrison Yuezhou, and Yun led two thousand men there ahead of the main force.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改臨江新淦丞。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was made assistant magistrate of Xingan in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xingan in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 縣新被兵，令不能支，沿江撫諭使張匯劾罷之，以運攝縣事。

translations.literal: The county had newly suffered warfare, and the magistrate could not sustain affairs. River-route Pacification Commissioner Zhang Hui impeached and removed him, and Yun was put in charge of county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The county had only recently been ravaged by war, and the magistrate could not cope. River-route Pacification Commissioner Zhang Hui impeached and removed him, and Yun was placed in charge of county affairs.

sentences.zh: 運撥煨燼，考版籍，正租賦，數月之間，弊除而民定。

translations.literal: Yun sorted through the smoldering ruins, examined the household registers, and corrected land tax and levies; within a few months abuses were removed and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yun sifted through the ashes of destruction, reviewed the household registers, and set right taxes and levies. Within a few months the abuses were gone and the people were settled.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，通判鼎州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was made vice-prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was appointed vice-prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊楊么、黃誠擁眾數萬，殘破城邑，跳梁湖北。

translations.literal: The bandits Yang Yao and Huang Cheng held several tens of thousands of men, ravaged cities and towns, and rampaged across Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels Yang Yao and Huang Cheng commanded tens of thousands of men, ravaged towns throughout the region, and ran riot across Hubei.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣張浚以都督董師，岳飛以招討舉兵擊之，賊率輕銳徑趨武溪南興，以臨鼎州，城中大震。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sent Zhang Jun as overall commander to direct the army and Yue Fei as pacification commissioner to raise troops against them. The bandits led their light elite straight toward Nanxing in Wuxi to threaten Dingzhou, and the city was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent Zhang Jun as overall commander to direct the campaign and Yue Fei as pacification commissioner to attack them. The rebels led their crack troops straight toward Nanxing in Wuxi to threaten Dingzhou, throwing the city into panic.

sentences.zh: 運與太守程昌宇勒兵登城，控扼上下，以張其勢，賊宵潰。

translations.literal: Yun and the prefect Cheng Changyu marshaled troops onto the walls, controlled the upper and lower reaches, and displayed their strength to the full; the bandits fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Prefect Cheng Changyu mustered troops onto the walls, held the upper and lower reaches of the river, and made a show of force so imposing that the rebels fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 澧賊雷德進柵險稱亂，帥檄運討之。

translations.literal: The Li bandit Lei Dejin fortified difficult terrain and declared rebellion; the commander issued an order for Yun to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The Li rebel Lei Dejin fortified rugged ground and raised rebellion. The commander ordered Yun to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 運將都統梁吉等率兵直搗其巢，破四十二柵，降其眾。

translations.literal: Yun led Commander-in-Chief Liang Ji and others in a direct assault on their lair, broke forty-two stockades, and received the surrender of their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yun led Commander-in-Chief Liang Ji and others in a direct assault on their stronghold, destroyed forty-two stockades, and accepted the surrender of their forces.

sentences.zh: 移貳濡須。

translations.literal: He was transferred as deputy administrator at Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as deputy administrator at Ruxu.

sentences.zh: 金人犯廬、壽等州，大將駐兵淮壖以拒之，運給餉未嘗乏絕。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked Luzhou, Shouzhou, and other prefectures. Great generals encamped on the Huai embankments to resist them, and Yun supplied provisions without ever falling short.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens attacked Luzhou, Shouzhou, and neighboring prefectures. The great generals encamped along the Huai to resist them, and Yun kept their supplies flowing without interruption.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以親老還江東，寓居鄱。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because his parents were elderly he returned to the Jiangdong region and took up residence at Po.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned to the Jiangdong region because his parents were elderly, and settled at Po.

sentences.zh: 既而丁母及父憂，服除，起知桂陽監。

translations.literal: He then entered mourning for his mother and father. When mourning ended he was recalled to serve as superintendent of Guiyang Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: He then went into mourning for his mother and father. When mourning ended he was recalled to serve as superintendent of the Guiyang Superintendency.

sentences.zh: 五月而境內稱治，與部使者奏升監為軍。

translations.literal: Within five months the territory within his borders was said to be well governed; together with the regional inspector he memorialized to elevate the superintendency to a military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within five months his jurisdiction was said to be well governed. Together with the regional inspector he memorialized to elevate the superintendency to a military prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大修庠序之教，祠漢以來守令有功德於桂陽者衛颯、唐羌等七人於學，刻《續顏氏家訓》、《四時纂要》等書，散之民間，使之修德而務本。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded instruction in the schools, enshrined in the academy seven prefects and magistrates since Han times who had merit in Guiyang, including Wei Sa and Tang Qiang, engraved books such as the Continued Yan Family Instructions and the Essentials of the Four Seasons, and distributed them among the people to make them cultivate virtue and attend to fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded school instruction, enshrined in the academy seven officials since Han times who had served Guiyang with merit, including Wei Sa and Tang Qiang, had books such as the Continued Yan Family Instructions and the Essentials of the Four Seasons carved and distributed among the people, urging them to cultivate virtue and attend to the fundamentals of life.

sentences.zh: 召入對，除知達州。

translations.literal: He was summoned for an audience and appointed prefect of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court for an audience and appointed prefect of Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 方大旱，入境而雨。

translations.literal: There was a great drought; when he entered the prefecture, rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought was afflicting the region; rain fell as soon as he entered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奏除病民五事。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remove five abuses harmful to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish five abuses that were harming the people.

sentences.zh: 召為度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and made Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 臨安樓店務錢歲三十餘萬緡，請以十萬歸省額。

translations.literal: The revenue of the Lou Shop Office in Lin'an amounted to more than three hundred thousand strings per year; he requested that one hundred thousand be returned to the provincial quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Lou Shop Office in Lin'an yielded more than three hundred thousand strings a year. He requested that one hundred thousand be returned to the provincial treasury quota.

sentences.zh: 戶部所儲三佛齊國所貢乳香九萬一千五百斤，直可百二十餘萬緡，請分送江、浙、荊湖漕司賣之，以糴軍餉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue had stored ninety-one thousand five hundred jin of frankincense presented by the Three Buddhas Qi state, worth more than twelve hundred thousand strings; he requested that it be sent in portions to the transport commissioners of Jiang, Zhe, and Jing-Hu to sell it and purchase army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue held ninety-one thousand five hundred jin of frankincense presented by the Three Buddhas Qi state, worth more than twelve hundred thousand strings. He proposed distributing it among the transport commissioners of Jiang, Zhe, and Jing-Hu to sell and use the proceeds to buy army provisions.

sentences.zh: 及陳諸路綱運七弊，懲革十術，遠近遞輸以均勞逸。

translations.literal: He also set forth seven abuses in the transport of tribute convoys on the various routes, proposed ten measures to reform and correct them, and arranged relay transport near and far to equalize labor and rest.
translations.idiomatic: He also identified seven abuses in tribute transport on the various routes, proposed ten corrective measures, and arranged relay transport over long and short distances to balance the burden of labor.

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All these measures were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were adopted and carried out.

sentences.zh: 兼樞密院檢詳，遷軍器監。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as reviewer in the Bureau of Military Affairs and was transferred to Director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as reviewer in the Bureau of Military Affairs and was promoted to Director of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 尋改大理少卿，請正兩浙鹽法，以寬私鬻之禁。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Vice Minister of Justice and requested correction of the salt laws in the two Zhe regions to relax the ban on private sale.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of Justice and proposed reforming the salt laws of the two Zhe circuits to ease the ban on private trade.

sentences.zh: 紹興永裕、昭慈二陵官地與民犬牙相入，請縣重價聽民持券獻納，以免誤犯之罪。

translations.literal: The official lands of the Yongyu and Zhaoci mausoleums of the Shaoxing reign interlocked with private holdings like dog's teeth; he requested that counties set high prices and allow the people to present deeds and pay in, so as to avoid the crime of inadvertent encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: The official lands of the Yongyu and Zhaoci imperial tombs intermingled with private holdings in a jagged patchwork. He proposed that counties set fair prices and allow holders to present their deeds and pay compensation, so that people would not be punished for inadvertent encroachment.

sentences.zh: 尤明於治獄，獄為之空。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in managing prisons, and the prisons were emptied on his account.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at managing legal cases, and the prisons were emptied under his administration.

sentences.zh: 拜刑部侍郎，言：「諸斥逐累赦未還者，宜從湔洗。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and said: "All those expelled and banished who, despite repeated amnesties, have not yet returned ought to be granted cleansing and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and said, "All those exiled and banished who, despite repeated amnesties, have not yet been allowed to return ought to be granted rehabilitation.

sentences.zh: 諸申請條製，多重復牴牾，失於太煩。

translations.literal: The various regulations governing petitions are largely redundant and contradictory, failing through excessive complexity.
translations.idiomatic: The various regulations governing petitions are riddled with redundancy and contradiction and have become excessively burdensome.

sentences.zh: 諸編置不以赦原、不以蔭論之類，失於太重。

translations.literal: The various categories of registered punishment not subject to amnesty and not subject to hereditary privilege are excessively severe.
translations.idiomatic: The various categories of registered offenders not eligible for amnesty or hereditary privilege are excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 外路刑獄三經翻異，移送大理，刀鋸數施，非所以示遠。

translations.literal: When criminal cases in the outer circuits are thrice reversed on appeal and transferred to the Court of Judicial Review, execution by blade and saw is repeatedly applied—this is not the way to display authority to distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: When criminal cases in the provinces are reversed three times on appeal and transferred to the Court of Judicial Review, executions are repeatedly carried out—this is no way to display justice to the distant regions.

sentences.zh: 」及諸不便，皆從之。

translations.literal: " And on various other inconveniences—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " On these and other abuses, the court adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 又請廣儲蓄，興鼓鑄，修屯田，作鄉兵。

translations.literal: He also requested expanding storage, reviving coinage, restoring garrison colonies, and organizing local militia.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed expanding grain reserves, reviving minting, restoring garrison colonies, and organizing local militia.

sentences.zh: 亦皆聽納。

translations.literal: These too were all accepted.
translations.idiomatic: These proposals too were all accepted.

sentences.zh: 兼權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He concurrently held acting appointment as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時久雨傷蠶麥，及邊報有警，詔侍從臺諫陳弭災禦侮之策。

translations.literal: At that time prolonged rain harmed silkworms and wheat, and frontier reports brought alarms; the emperor ordered attendants and remonstrance officials to set forth strategies to quell disasters and repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains were damaging the silkworm and wheat crops, and alarming reports arrived from the frontier. The emperor ordered his attendants and remonstrance officials to propose strategies for averting disaster and repelling invasion.

sentences.zh: 運言：「天災人事，有甚可畏而不足畏者，視吾政之修不修；

translations.literal: Yun said: "Heavenly disasters and human affairs—there are things greatly to be feared that are not truly to be feared, depending on whether our government is well ordered or not;
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Heavenly disasters and human affairs alike contain much that seems terrifying yet is not truly to be feared, depending on whether our government is well ordered;

sentences.zh: 有甚可憂而不足憂者，視吾自治之善不善。

translations.literal: there are things greatly to be worried over that are not truly to be worried over, depending on whether our self-governance is good or not.
translations.idiomatic: and much that seems worrisome yet is not truly to be worried over, depending on whether we govern ourselves well.

sentences.zh: 」及宜邊淮建三大鎮以守之。

translations.literal: " He also said that along the Huai frontier three great garrison commands ought to be established for defense.
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued that three great garrison commands ought to be established along the Huai frontier for defense.

sentences.zh: 會金人渝盟，特遷戶部侍郎，以專饋餉。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens violated the treaty, he was specially promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue to specialize in supplying provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens broke the treaty, he was specially promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue with sole responsibility for supplying the armies.

sentences.zh: 丞相陳康伯議遣李寶自四明控制海道，眾論紛紜，運直入贊決，以為上策，金人果敗走。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Chen Kangbo proposed dispatching Li Bao from Siming to control the sea route; opinion was divided, but Yun went in directly to endorse and decide the matter, holding it the best strategy—and the Jurchens were indeed defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Chen Kangbo proposed sending Li Bao from Siming to control the sea lanes. Opinion was divided, but Yun went straight in to endorse the plan as the best strategy. The Jurchens were indeed defeated and driven off.

sentences.zh: 因上疏：「乞降詔撫將士，蠲租賦，遣信使，結豪傑，堅城守，督漢中將士趨關陝以制其後。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial: "I beg that an edict be issued to comfort officers and soldiers, remit taxes and levies, dispatch trusted envoys, win over heroes, hold fast to city defenses, and urge the officers and soldiers of Hanzhong to hurry toward Guanzhong and Shaanxi to pin the enemy from behind.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "I beg that an edict be issued to comfort the troops, remit taxes and levies, dispatch trusted envoys, rally local heroes, hold the cities firm, and urge the forces of Hanzhong to advance toward Guanzhong and Shaanxi to threaten the enemy's rear.

sentences.zh: 置四鎮三帥於兩淮、襄漢之間以為內固，以圖進取。

translations.literal: Establish four commands and three commanders between the two Huai regions and Xiang-Han as an inner bulwark, in order to plan advance and recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Establish four commands and three commanders between the two Huai regions and the Xiang-Han area as an inner bulwark, and thereby plan for advance and recovery.

sentences.zh: 」以御營隨軍都轉運使從上勞師江上。

translations.literal: " As Director of the Imperial Camp's Army Transport he accompanied the emperor in reviewing the troops on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: " As Director of the Imperial Camp's Army Transport he accompanied the emperor in reviewing the troops along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及駕還，因入對，固請補外。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he took the occasion of an audience to firmly request an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, he sought an audience and firmly requested an appointment outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃授集英殿修撰，出知太平州。

translations.literal: He was then given the post of Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Excellence and sent out as prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Excellence and sent out as prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 當兵饑疾癘之餘，殫勞徠安輯之方，嚴斥堠攻守之備。

translations.literal: In the aftermath of war, famine, and pestilence, he exhausted every method to encourage settlement and restore order, and strictly maintained beacon towers and preparations for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war, famine, and pestilence, he exhausted every means to encourage resettlement and restore order, and strictly maintained the beacon towers and defenses.

sentences.zh: 理財賦，造戰艦，繕甲兵，申禁令，民賴以安。

translations.literal: He put finances and levies in order, built warships, repaired armor and weapons, and enforced prohibitions; the people relied on this and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He put finances and taxes in order, built warships, repaired armor and weapons, and enforced the laws. The people found security in his administration.

sentences.zh: 孝宗既受禪，運亦請老，以敷文閣待制提舉江州太平興國宮，尋授廣東經略，不赴，乃復祠祿。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaozong had received the abdication, Yun also requested retirement and was made Drafter-at-Large of the Fuwen Pavilion to superintend the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou. Shortly afterward he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Guangdong but did not go; he then resumed a stipendary post.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozong had ascended the throne, Yun also requested retirement. He was made Drafter-at-Large of the Fuwen Pavilion to superintend the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou. He was soon appointed Pacification Commissioner of Guangdong but declined to go, and thereafter held a stipendary post.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，鄱大饑，運首發粟二千石以振之，自是民爭出粟以濟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao, Poyang suffered a great famine. Yun took the lead in distributing two thousand shi of grain to relieve it; from then on the people vied to contribute grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qiandao, Poyang was stricken by severe famine. Yun was the first to release two thousand shi of grain for relief, and thereafter the people competed to bring forth their own grain to aid the hungry.

sentences.zh: 連上章致政，不許，以疾卒。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement; this was not granted, and he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial asking to retire from office, but permission was denied, and he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈少師、左光祿大夫，官其後三人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Junior Preceptor and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and three of his descendants were given official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Junior Preceptor and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and official rank was granted to three of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiading, he was posthumously granted the title Commissioner with the Ceremonial Honors of a Grand General of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiading, he was posthumously ennobled with the rank of Commissioner with the Ceremonial Honors of a Grand General of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 柳約，字元禮，秀州華亭人。

translations.literal: Liu Yue, courtesy name Yuanli, was a native of Huating in Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue, styled Yuanli, was a native of Huating in Xiu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年上舍進士，試中學官，為霸州教授。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan he passed the upper-dormitory jinshi examination, passed the examination for academy officials, and was appointed instructor in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daguan he earned his jinshi degree through the upper dormitory and passed the examination for academy officials, after which he was appointed instructor in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 徙睦州，入為辟雍正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Mizhou, then entered the capital as deputy director of the Bureau for Recruiting Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Mizhou, then recalled to the capital to serve as deputy director of the Bureau for Recruiting Worthies.

sentences.zh: 遷博士，改宣議郎，充廣親宅宗子博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to erudite, changed to Gentlemen for Promoting Harmony, and appointed erudite for imperial clansmen in the Broad Affection Residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite, given the rank of Gentlemen for Promoting Harmony, and appointed erudite for imperial clansmen in the Broad Affection Residence.

sentences.zh: 約深於經學，屬辭粹微，大為學者師慕。

translations.literal: Yue was deeply versed in classical learning; his literary composition was refined and subtle, and he was greatly admired as a teacher by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was deeply learned in the classics, and his prose was refined and subtle; scholars looked to him as a master and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 提舉福建鹽事，召對，論內外學政，次乞罷內外官到堂日投牒求官，以厚風俗。

translations.literal: As supervisor of salt affairs in Fujian, he was summoned for an audience, discussed education policy at court and in the provinces, and then requested the abolition of the practice whereby officials submitted petitions seeking appointments on their day of attendance at court, so as to strengthen public morals.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising salt affairs in Fujian, he was summoned to audience. He spoke on education policy at court and in the provinces, then petitioned to abolish the custom of officials submitting petitions for office on their day of court attendance, arguing that this would help restore proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 授秘書省校書郎，進著作佐郎、徽州司錄，改通判宿州，召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed collator in the Secretariat, promoted to assistant compiler and judicial recorder in Huizhou, changed to vice prefect of Suzhou, and summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator in the Secretariat, then promoted to assistant compiler and judicial recorder in Huizhou, later made vice prefect of Suzhou, and finally summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，兼權殿中侍御史，論三鎮不可棄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era he concurrently served as acting palace attendant censor and argued that the Three Garrisons must not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era he also served as acting palace attendant censor, where he argued that the Three Garrisons must not be surrendered.

sentences.zh: 改尚書工部員外郎，進左司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to outer-section member of the Ministry of Works and promoted to outer-section member of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer-section member of the Ministry of Works and then promoted to outer-section member of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 父憂去官，服除，以直顯謨閣充御營司參謀官，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He left office upon his father's death; when the mourning period ended, he served as staff officer in the Imperial Camp Office with the appointment of Direct Associate of the Hall for Manifesting Counsel, and was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his father. When the mourning period ended, he was appointed staff officer in the Imperial Camp Office with the title Direct Associate of the Hall for Manifesting Counsel, and was later promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高宗將幸平江，約疏言兵可進，毋退以示怯於敵。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to travel to Pingjiang, Yue submitted a memorial stating that the army could advance and should not retreat, lest this show the enemy cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was preparing to travel to Pingjiang, Yue submitted a memorial urging that the army should advance rather than withdraw, warning that retreat would only display fear before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 乃以直龍圖閣知台州，未赴，徙嚴州，兼浙西兵馬都監、節制管內軍馬。

translations.literal: He was then appointed prefect of Taizhou with the appointment of Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall; before he took up the post he was transferred to Yanzhou, concurrently serving as military supervisor of Zhexi and commander of armed forces within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Taizhou with the title Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall. Before he could take up the post, he was transferred to Yanzhou, where he also served as military supervisor of western Zhejiang and commander of the armed forces within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 當是時，金人大入，杜充擁眾北去，列郡震恐，莫有奔問官守者。

translations.literal: At that time the Jurchens invaded on a great scale; Du Chong led his forces north in flight; the prefectures were shaken with terror, and none came to the aid of the officials holding their posts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jurchens swept in with overwhelming force. Du Chong fled north with his troops, and the surrounding prefectures were gripped by panic; none sent help to the officials who remained at their posts.

sentences.zh: 約於橫潰中屹保孤城，悉力捍禦。

translations.literal: Amid the general collapse, Yue stood firm and held the isolated city, exerting all his strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: While all around him collapsed into chaos, Yue held his isolated city unyielding and poured every ounce of strength into its defense.

sentences.zh: 境內按堵，則慨然上書，請糾合諸郡克復吳會。

translations.literal: Once the territory within his jurisdiction was secure, he submitted an impassioned memorial requesting that the prefectures be rallied to recover the Wu and Yue region.
translations.idiomatic: When order had been restored within his jurisdiction, he submitted an impassioned memorial calling for the prefectures to be rallied together to recover the lands of Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其忠，進右文殿修撰，守郡如故。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and promoted him to compiler of the Right Hall for Cultivating Culture, while he continued to hold his prefectural post as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his loyalty and promoted him to compiler of the Right Hall for Cultivating Culture, while he continued to govern his prefecture as before.

sentences.zh: 詔以軍興費出無藝，吏慢弗虔，柳約獨謹賦輸，率先程督，進秩一等。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because military expenses had no fixed limit and officials were negligent and lax, Liu Yue alone submitted taxes with scrupulous care and took the lead in enforcing schedules; he was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that with military expenses unlimited and officials slack and negligent, Liu Yue alone submitted his taxes with scrupulous diligence and personally enforced the collection schedule. For this he was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「約郡當兵衝，而能不辭難、不避事，益嚴列柵，保綏一方，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Another edict read: "Yue's prefecture lies on the main military route, yet he has not shirked hardship or avoided responsibility; he has further strengthened the palisades and secured peace in his region. We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "Yue's prefecture stands on the front line of war, yet he has neither shirked hardship nor avoided responsibility. He has strengthened the defenses and brought stability to his region. We commend him highly.

sentences.zh: 其以約充集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: Let Yue be appointed compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence."
translations.idiomatic: Let Yue be appointed compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence."

sentences.zh: 」召入對，獎勞再三，擢權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience, repeatedly praised and rewarded, and promoted to acting vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience, praised and rewarded again and again, and promoted to acting vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 約於是感激盡言，凡例外宣索，皆執奏不進。

translations.literal: Yue, moved by gratitude, spoke forthrightly on all matters; whenever there were extraordinary requisitions from the palace, he memorialized in opposition and refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Yue now spoke without reserve. Whenever the court issued extraordinary requisitions, he memorialized in protest and refused to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 論吳幵等罪未正，非所以厲臣節；

translations.literal: He argued that the crimes of Wu Kai and others had not yet been properly punished, which was no way to encourage ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the crimes of Wu Kai and his associates had not yet been properly punished—a failure that could only undermine the integrity of the official class.

sentences.zh: 諸大將提兵入覲，各名其家，將有尾大不掉之患，皆人不敢言者。

translations.literal: He also said that when the great generals led their troops to court audience, each named his own household estate, and there would be the danger that the tail grows too heavy to wag—matters that others dared not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that when the great generals marched their armies to court, each proclaimed his own private estate by name, creating the danger that the tail would grow too heavy to control—things no one else dared to say aloud.

sentences.zh: 又言：「軍興科需百出，望官戶名田過制者，與編戶均一科敷。

translations.literal: He further said: "With military levies multiplying in every direction, I ask that registered households whose land holdings exceed the prescribed limit be taxed at the same rates as ordinary households.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed: "With military levies multiplying on every side, let registered households whose land holdings exceed the legal limit be taxed at the same rates as ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 請增諸路酒錢，其半令提刑司樁管，以備軍費。

translations.literal: I request that the wine tax be increased in each circuit, with half of the proceeds placed under the custody of the judicial-intendant offices to provide for military expenses."
translations.idiomatic: I also request that the wine tax be increased in each circuit, with half the proceeds held in reserve by the judicial-intendant offices to meet military expenses."

sentences.zh: 」皆從之。

translations.literal: All of these proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 會高麗請修貢，議遣使報聘，上顧廷臣無出約右，加試戶部侍郎充其選，且將大用。

translations.literal: When Goryeo requested the renewal of tribute missions, the court deliberated sending an envoy in return; the emperor looked among the court officials and found none superior to Yue. He added a probationary appointment as vice minister of revenue to qualify him for the mission and was about to give him greater responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo requested the resumption of tribute missions, the court debated sending an envoy in reply. The emperor surveyed the officials at court and found none better suited than Yue. He gave him a probationary appointment as vice minister of revenue to qualify him for the mission and was preparing to entrust him with greater duties.

sentences.zh: 當路忌之，諷言者誣以事，罷為提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Those in power envied him and incited remonstrating officials to frame him with false charges; he was dismissed and made supervisor of the Taiping View.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power grew jealous and prompted remonstrating officials to fabricate charges against him. He was dismissed and appointed supervisor of the Taiping View.

sentences.zh: 居七年，復秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: After seven years he was restored as compiler in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years he was restored to his post as compiler in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 金人歸侵疆，起知蔡州，被命而往，一無顧避。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens returned the occupied territories, he was appointed prefect of Caizhou; he received the order and went without the slightest hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens returned the occupied territories, he was appointed prefect of Caizhou. He accepted the commission and set out without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 既而金人渝平，傳檄河南，守臣皆舉城降，約獨遣使數輩於武昌，得報而後返。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens violated the peace agreement and issued a proclamation to Henan; the defending officials all surrendered their cities, but Yue alone sent several envoys to Wuchang and only returned after receiving a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jurchens broke the peace and issued a proclamation across Henan. The defending officials surrendered their cities one after another, but Yue alone dispatched several envoys to Wuchang and did not return until he had received a response.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以敷文閣待制食祠祿。

translations.literal: Not long after, he served as academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture on temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture, drawing a stipend from a sinecure temple post.

sentences.zh: 十有五年，卒。

translations.literal: Fifteen years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈四官。

translations.literal: Four official ranks were granted posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted four ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 約天性至孝，母病甚，泣禱於天，願損壽以益親壽。

translations.literal: Yue was filial by nature to the utmost degree. When his mother fell gravely ill, he wept and prayed to Heaven, wishing to shorten his own life to extend his parent's.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was profoundly filial by nature. When his mother fell gravely ill, he wept and prayed to Heaven, offering to shorten his own life in exchange for hers.

sentences.zh: 母尋愈，約竟先母兩月卒。

translations.literal: His mother soon recovered, but Yue died two months before her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother soon recovered, but Yue himself died two months before she did.

sentences.zh: 李舜臣

translations.literal: Li Shunchen
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunchen

sentences.zh: 李舜臣，字子思，隆州井研人。

translations.literal: Li Shunchen, courtesy name Zisi, was a native of Jingyan in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunchen, styled Zisi, was a native of Jingyan in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生四年知讀書，八歲能屬文，少長通古今，推迹興廢，洞見根本，慨然有志於天下。

translations.literal: At the age of four he knew how to read; at eight he could compose essays. As he grew he mastered past and present, traced the rise and fall of states, saw through to root causes, and was moved to set his heart on the affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At four he could read; at eight he could compose essays. As he matured he mastered the history of past and present, traced the rise and fall of states to their roots, and resolved to devote himself to the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 紹興末，張浚視師江、淮，舜臣應詔上書，言：「乘輿不出，無以定大計，宜徙幸武昌。

translations.literal: Late in the Shaoxing era, when Zhang Jun commanded the armies on the Yangzi and Huai, Shunchen responded to an imperial call for memorials, saying: "If the imperial carriage does not move, there is no way to settle the great plan; it should be moved to Wuchang."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shaoxing era, when Zhang Jun took command on the Yangzi and Huai fronts, Shunchen submitted a memorial in response to an imperial call, arguing: "Unless the emperor himself moves, no great strategy can be settled—the court should relocate to Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「江東六朝皆嘗取勝北方，不肯乘機爭天下，宜為今日監。

translations.literal: He also said: "The six dynasties of Jiangdong all once prevailed over the north yet refused to seize the moment to contend for the realm; this should serve as a lesson for today."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The six dynasties of Jiangdong all once held the advantage over the north, yet none seized the moment to contest for the realm. Let that be a warning for our own day."

sentences.zh: 」著《江東勝後之鑒》十篇上之。

translations.literal: He composed ten chapters entitled 《Lessons from Victory in Jiangdong》 and submitted them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He composed ten chapters entitled 《Lessons from Victory in Jiangdong》 and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 中乾道二年進士第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiandao he earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷既罷兵，而為相者益不厭天下望。

translations.literal: At that time the court had already ceased military operations, yet those serving as chief ministers were ever less responsive to the hopes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already ceased military operations, yet the chief ministers grew ever more deaf to the nation's hopes.

sentences.zh: 舜臣對策，論金人世仇，無可和之義，宰輔大臣不當以奉行文字為職業。

translations.literal: In his examination response Shunchen argued that the Jurchens were the dynasty's hereditary enemy and that there was no grounds for peace, and that chief ministers and great officials ought not to make their profession the mere execution of written orders.
translations.idiomatic: In his palace examination response, Shunchen argued that the Jurchens were the dynasty's hereditary enemy and that peace was unthinkable, and that chief ministers should not reduce their office to the routine execution of written orders.

sentences.zh: 考官惡焉，絀下第，調邛州安仁縣主簿。

translations.literal: The examiners took offense; he was demoted in rank and assigned as chief clerk of Anren County in Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners took offense. He was placed in the lower tier of graduates and assigned as chief clerk of Anren County in Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，饑民千百持鉏棘大呼，響震邑市，令懼閉門。

translations.literal: That year there was a great famine; hundreds of hungry people, carrying hoes and thorn branches, shouted loudly, their voices shaking the town market. The magistrate, in fear, shut his gates.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck. Hundreds of starving people, carrying hoes and thorn branches, raised a clamor that shook the market town. The magistrate, terrified, barred his gates.

sentences.zh: 舜臣曰：「此非盜也，何懼為？

translations.literal: Shunchen said: "These are not bandits—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Shunchen said, "These are not bandits. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」亟出慰勞遣之。

translations.literal: He immediately went out to comfort and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: He went out at once to comfort them and send them on their way.

sentences.zh: 教授成都府。

translations.literal: He served as instructor in Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as instructor in Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時虞允文撫師關上，辟置幕府，用舉者改宣教郎、知饒州德興縣，專尚風化。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Yunwen commanded the army on the frontier passes and recruited Shunchen into his staff; on the recommendation of his sponsor he was changed to Gentlemen for Promoting Education and appointed magistrate of Dexing County in Rao Prefecture, where he devoted himself chiefly to moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Yunwen held command on the frontier passes and recruited Shunchen into his staff. On his sponsor's recommendation he was given the rank of Gentlemen for Promoting Education and appointed magistrate of Dexing County in Rao Prefecture, where he devoted himself above all to moral reform.

sentences.zh: 民有母子昆弟之訟連年不決，為陳慈孝友恭之道，遂為母子兄弟如初。

translations.literal: There was a lawsuit between mother and son and between brothers that had remained unresolved for years; he expounded the way of kindness, filial piety, fraternity, and respect, and mother and sons and brothers were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: A lawsuit pitting mother against son and brother against brother had dragged on for years. He expounded the virtues of kindness, filial piety, fraternity, and respect, and mother, sons, and brothers were reconciled as before.

sentences.zh: 間詣學講說，邑士皆稱「蜀先生」。

translations.literal: From time to time he visited the school to lecture, and the local scholars all called him "Master Shu."
translations.idiomatic: He would occasionally visit the school to lecture, and the local scholars all called him "Master Shu."

sentences.zh: 罷百姓預貸，償前官積逋逾三萬緡。

translations.literal: He abolished advance loans to the people and repaid more than thirty thousand strings of accumulated arrears left by his predecessor.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished advance loans to the people and repaid more than thirty thousand strings in accumulated arrears left by his predecessor.

sentences.zh: 民病差役，舜臣勸糾諸鄉，以稅數低昂定役期久近為義役。

translations.literal: The people suffered under the corvée system of labor service; Shunchen urged the townships to reform it, fixing the length of service obligations according to whether tax quotas were high or low.
translations.idiomatic: The people were burdened by the corvée system. Shunchen urged the townships to reform it, setting the length of service obligations according to whether a household's tax quota was high or low.

sentences.zh: 期年役成，民大便利。

translations.literal: Within a year the reform was complete, and the people found it greatly convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the reform was complete, and the people found the new arrangement a great relief.

sentences.zh: 銀坑罷雖久，小戶猶敷銀本錢，官為償之。

translations.literal: Although the silver mines had long been closed, small households were still assessed silver-capital fees; the government repaid these on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Though the silver mines had long been shut down, small households were still being charged silver-capital fees. The government repaid these on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 天申大禮助賞及軍器所需，皆不以煩民。

translations.literal: For the rewards granted on the Grand Ceremony of Heavenly Submission and for military equipment needs, he never troubled the people.
translations.idiomatic: When funds were needed for the rewards of the Grand Ceremony of Heavenly Submission and for military equipment, he never imposed the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 幹辦諸司審計司，遷宗正寺主簿，重修《裕陵玉牒》。

translations.literal: He served in the Audit Office of the Various Bureaus, was promoted to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, and revised the 《Imperial Genealogy of Yuzong》.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Audit Office of the Various Bureaus, was promoted to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, and undertook a revision of the 《Imperial Genealogy of Yuzong》.

sentences.zh: 當曾布、呂惠卿初用，必謹書，或謂非執政除免，格不應書。

translations.literal: When Zeng Bu and Lü Huiqing were first appointed, he always recorded it with care. Some said that since these were not appointments or dismissals made by the chief administrators, the regulations did not require recording.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Bu and Lü Huiqing were first appointed, he always recorded the fact with scrupulous care. Some argued that since these were not appointments or dismissals made by the chief administrators, the regulations did not require such entries.

sentences.zh: 舜臣曰：「治忽所關，何可拘常法。

translations.literal: Shunchen said: "This bears on the rise and fall of good government—how can one be bound by routine rules?"
translations.idiomatic: Shunchen replied, "This bears on the rise and fall of good government. How can one be bound by routine rules?"

sentences.zh: 」他所筆削類此。

translations.literal: His editorial judgments elsewhere were of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: His editorial judgments elsewhere followed the same principle.

sentences.zh: 尤邃於《易》，嘗曰：「《易》起於畫，理事象數，皆因畫以見，舍畫而論，非《易》也。

translations.literal: He was especially profound in the 《Book of Changes》, and once said: "The 《Changes》 arises from the trigrams; principle, affairs, images, and numbers all become visible through the trigrams. To discuss the 《Changes》 apart from the trigrams is not the 《Changes》."
translations.idiomatic: He was especially profound in the 《Book of Changes》, and once said: "The 《Changes》 begins with the trigrams. Principle, affairs, images, and numbers all become visible through them. To discuss the 《Changes》 apart from the trigrams is not to discuss the 《Changes》 at all."

sentences.zh: 畫從中起，乾坤中畫為誠敬，坎離中畫為誠明。

translations.literal: "The lines proceed from the center: in Qian and Kun the central line signifies sincerity and reverence; in Kan and Li the central line signifies sincerity and clarity."
translations.idiomatic: "The lines proceed from the center: in Qian and Kun the central line signifies sincerity and reverence; in Kan and Li it signifies sincerity and clarity."

sentences.zh: 」著《本傳》三十三篇。

translations.literal: He composed thirty-three chapters of the 《Original Transmission》.
translations.idiomatic: He composed thirty-three chapters of the 《Original Transmission》.

sentences.zh: 朱熹晚歲，每為學者稱之。

translations.literal: In his later years Zhu Xi often praised him to his students.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Zhu Xi often spoke of him with praise to his students.

sentences.zh: 所著書《群經義》八卷、《書小傳》四卷、文集三十卷、《家塾編次論語》五卷、《鏤玉餘功錄》二卷。

translations.literal: His written works included eight volumes of 《The Meaning of the Classics》, four volumes of 《Brief Commentary on the Documents》, thirty volumes of collected writings, five volumes of 《Family School Arrangement of the Analects》, and two volumes of the 《Record of Carving Jade's Remaining Achievement》.
translations.idiomatic: His written works included eight volumes of 《The Meaning of the Classics》, four volumes of 《Brief Commentary on the Documents》, thirty volumes of collected writings, five volumes of 《Family School Arrangement of the Analects》, and two volumes of the 《Record of Carving Jade's Remaining Achievement》.

sentences.zh: 子心傳、道傳、性傳。

translations.literal: His sons were Xinchuan, Daochuan, and Xingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xinchuan, Daochuan, and Xingchuan.

sentences.zh: 以性傳官二府，贈太師、追封崇國公。

translations.literal: Through Xingchuan's office in the Two Departments, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Through Xingchuan's service in the Two Departments, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 孫逢吉

translations.literal: Sun Fengji
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengji

sentences.zh: 孫逢吉，字從之，吉州龍泉人也。

translations.literal: Sun Fengji, courtesy name Congzhi, was a native of Longquan in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengji, styled Congzhi, was a native of Longquan in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年進士第，授郴州司戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed revenue recorder in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he earned his jinshi degree and was appointed revenue recorder in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，太常黃鈞薦於丞相虞允文、梁克家，將處以學官，逢吉竟就常德教授以歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao, Huang Jun of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices recommended him to the chief ministers Yu Yunwen and Liang Kejia, who were about to appoint him to an academy post, but Fengji instead took up the post of instructor in Changde and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qiandao, Huang Jun of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices recommended him to Chief Ministers Yu Yunwen and Liang Kejia, who were preparing to appoint him to an academy post. Fengji instead accepted an appointment as instructor in Changde and returned home.

sentences.zh: 李燾、劉珙、鄭伯熊、劉焞相繼薦之，知萍鄉縣，以治最聞。

translations.literal: Li Tao, Liu Gong, Zheng Boxiong, and Liu Hun successively recommended him; he was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang County and became known for outstanding governance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao, Liu Gong, Zheng Boxiong, and Liu Hun recommended him in turn. He was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang County and became renowned for the excellence of his administration.

sentences.zh: 除諸軍審計司、國子博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed to the Audit Office of the Various Armies and to erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Audit Office of the Various Armies and to erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 遷司農寺丞兼實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, concurrently serving as collator in the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, concurrently serving as collator in the Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，遷秘書郎兼皇子嘉王府直講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was promoted to secretary and concurrently direct lecturer in the Hall of the Heir Apparent Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he was promoted to secretary and concurrently appointed direct lecturer in the Hall of the Heir Apparent Jia.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月，雷雪之沴交作，詔求直言，疏八事：去蔽諛、親講讀、伸論駁、崇氣節、省用度、惜名器、拔材武、飭戎備。

translations.literal: In the second year, in the second month of spring, thunder and snow calamities occurred together; an edict called for forthright speech. He submitted eight points: remove obstruction and flattery, attend closely to lectures and study, allow debate and rebuttal, honor moral integrity, reduce expenditures, cherish official titles, promote men of talent and martial ability, and strengthen military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, in the second month of spring, thunder and snow struck together as omens of disorder. An edict called for forthright counsel, and he submitted eight recommendations: remove obstruction and flattery, attend closely to lectures and study, allow open debate and rebuttal, honor moral integrity, reduce expenditures, treat official titles with respect, promote men of talent and martial ability, and strengthen military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 擢為右正言，建言：「都城之民，安居憚徙。

translations.literal: He was promoted to remonstrating official of the Right and submitted a memorial: "The people of the capital city dwell in comfort and dread being moved.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrating official of the Right and submitted a memorial: "The people of the capital dwell in comfort and dread being uprooted.

sentences.zh: 宗戚營繕寖廣，每建一第，撤民居數百，咨怨者多。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and consorts have steadily expanded their estates; each time a mansion is built, hundreds of common dwellings are demolished, and complaints are many."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and consorts have steadily expanded their estates. Each time a mansion is built, hundreds of common dwellings are torn down, and the complaints are many."

sentences.zh: 」時親王方更造樓觀未已，聞之，亟令罷役。

translations.literal: At that time an imperial prince was still building towers and pavilions without cease; on hearing this he immediately ordered the work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an imperial prince was still building towers and pavilions without pause. On hearing the memorial, he immediately ordered the work halted.

sentences.zh: 浙漕沈詵見逢吉，謝曰：「非正言，漕計殆不可支。

translations.literal: Shen Chuan, transport commissioner of Zhejiang, met Fengji and thanked him, saying: "Were it not for the remonstrating official, the transport accounts would scarcely have been sustainable."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chuan, transport commissioner of Zhejiang, sought out Fengji and thanked him, saying, "Were it not for the remonstrating official, the transport accounts would scarcely have held."

sentences.zh: 」初，工部侍郎兼知臨安府潘景珪結貴幸以進，司諫鄧馹屢疏其罪，景珪反以計傾之，除馹匠監。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pan Jinggui, vice minister of works and concurrent prefect of Lin'an, had advanced through connections with the powerful and favored; remonstrating official Deng Ji had repeatedly memorialized against his crimes, but Jinggui in turn plotted to ruin him and had him appointed supervisor of the Artisans' Office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pan Jinggui, vice minister of works and concurrent prefect of Lin'an, had risen through connections with the powerful and favored. Remonstrating official Deng Ji had repeatedly memorialized against his crimes, but Jinggui retaliated with a plot to destroy him and had him appointed supervisor of the Artisans' Office.

sentences.zh: 逢吉曰：「優遷其官而罷言職，後來者且以言為戒。

translations.literal: Fengji said: "To promote his rank while removing him from remonstrating office will teach those who follow to treat speech as something to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: Fengji said, "To promote his rank while stripping him of his remonstrating office will teach those who follow to fear speaking out."

sentences.zh: 」兩疏乞收馹新命，不報；

translations.literal: He submitted two memorials requesting the revocation of Ji's new appointment, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted two memorials requesting that Ji's new appointment be revoked, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 並劾景珪脅持臺諫，蔑視朝綱，景珪遂罷。

translations.literal: He also impeached Jinggui for coercing the censorial and remonstrating offices and treating the court's authority with contempt; Jinggui was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Jinggui for coercing the censorial and remonstrating offices and treating the court's authority with contempt. Jinggui was thereupon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 在諫垣七十日，章二十上，詞旨剴切，皆人所難言者。

translations.literal: During seventy days in the remonstrating office he submitted twenty memorials; their language was incisive, and all touched on matters others found difficult to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: In seventy days in the remonstrating office he submitted twenty memorials—incisive in language and all addressing matters others found too dangerous to speak of.

sentences.zh: 改國子司業，求去，為湖南提刑。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of education in the Directorate and requested leave, becoming judicial intendant of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of education in the Directorate, then requested leave from court and was appointed judicial intendant of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以秘書監召，兼吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director of the Secretariat, concurrently serving as vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as director of the Secretariat, concurrently holding the post of vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 俄為孝宗攢宮按行使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed commissioner for the inspection of Xiaozong's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed commissioner for the inspection of Xiaozong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 朱熹在經筵持論切直，小人共不便，潛激上怒，中批與祠。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi spoke forthrightly in the Classics Lecture Hall; petty men together found this inconvenient and secretly incited the emperor's anger; an imperial rescript in the middle of proceedings dismissed him to a sinecure temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi spoke with uncompromising directness in the Classics Lecture Hall. Petty men found this intolerable and secretly stirred the emperor's anger; a rescript issued in mid-session dismissed him to a sinecure temple post.

sentences.zh: 劉光祖與逢吉同在講筵，吏請曰：「今日某侍郎輪講，以疾告，孫侍郎居次，請代之。

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu and Fengji were both in the lecture hall when an attendant asked: "Today a certain vice minister is scheduled to lecture but has reported illness. Vice Minister Sun is next in order—may he take his place?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu and Fengji were both in the lecture hall when an attendant asked, "The vice minister scheduled to lecture today has reported illness. Vice Minister Sun is next in order—may he take his place?"

sentences.zh: 」逢吉曰：「常所講《論語》，今安得即有講義？

translations.literal: Fengji said: "We ordinarily lecture on the 《Analects》—how can I produce a prepared lecture on the spot?"
translations.idiomatic: Fengji said, "We ordinarily lecture on the 《Analects》. How can I produce a prepared lecture at a moment's notice?"

sentences.zh: 」已而問某侍郎講義安在，取觀之，則講《詩·權輿篇》，刺康公與賢者有始而無終，與逐朱熹事相類，逢吉欣然代之講。

translations.literal: He then asked where the vice minister's lecture notes were, took them to read, and found that the lecture was on the 《Ode "The Locust Tree"》 in the 《Book of Poetry》, which satirizes Duke Kang of Wei and worthy men who have a beginning but no end—a parallel to the dismissal of Zhu Xi—and Fengji gladly took his place to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked where the vice minister's lecture notes were. On reading them he found the lecture was on the 《Ode "The Locust Tree"》 in the 《Book of Poetry》—a satire on Duke Kang of Wei and on worthy men who begin well but finish badly, paralleling Zhu Xi's dismissal. Fengji gladly stepped in to deliver the lecture.

sentences.zh: 因於上前爭論甚苦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he argued strenuously before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he argued strenuously before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朱熹言多不可用用。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Most of what Zhu Xi says cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Most of what Zhu Xi says is of no use."

sentences.zh: 」逢吉曰：「熹議祧廟與臣不合，他所言皆正，未見其不可用。

translations.literal: Fengji said: "On the question of the spirit temple, Xi and I disagree, but everything else he says is correct—I do not see that he cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Fengji said, "I disagree with Xi on the ancestral temple, but everything else he says is correct. I see no reason he should be dismissed as unusable."

sentences.zh: 」寖失上意。

translations.literal: Gradually he lost the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he lost the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 會彭龜年論韓侂胄專僭，出補郡。

translations.literal: At that time Peng Guinian spoke against Han Tuozhou's usurpation of authority and was sent out to fill a post in a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Peng Guinian criticized Han Tuozhou for monopolizing power and was sent out to serve as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 逢吉入疏曰：「道德崇重，陛下所敬禮者無若朱熹，志節端亮，陛下所委信者無若彭龜年。

translations.literal: Fengji submitted a memorial saying: "In moral weight none whom Your Majesty honors surpasses Zhu Xi; in integrity and uprightness none whom Your Majesty trusts surpasses Peng Guinian.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji submitted a memorial saying, "In moral stature, no one Your Majesty honors surpasses Zhu Xi; in integrity and uprightness, no one Your Majesty trusts surpasses Peng Guinian.

sentences.zh: 熹既以論侂胄去，龜年復以論侂胄絀，臣恐賢者皆無固志。

translations.literal: Since Xi was removed for criticizing Tuozhou and Guinian was again demoted for criticizing Tuozhou, I fear worthy men will all lose firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xi was removed for criticizing Tuozhou and Guinian was demoted again for the same reason, I fear worthy men will lose the will to stand firm.

sentences.zh: 陛下所用皆庸鄙憸薄之徒，何以立國？

translations.literal: Those Your Majesty employs are all vulgar, base, crafty, and mean sort—how can the state be established?"
translations.idiomatic: Those Your Majesty employs are all vulgar, base, crafty, and mean—how can the state endure?"

sentences.zh: 」侂胄見而惡之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou saw this and hated it.
