translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou saw the memorial and hated it.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚既罷，侂胄專國。

translations.literal: After Chancellor Zhao Ruyu was dismissed, Tuozhou monopolized state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Chancellor Zhao Ruyu was dismissed, Tuozhou monopolized the government.

sentences.zh: 一日從臣扈從重華宮，上行禮畢，駕興，扈從者出宮門上馬，忽傳呼侂胄至，扈從者卻入，斂板甚恭。

translations.literal: One day the attendant ministers were escorting the emperor at Chonghua Palace. When the emperor had finished the rites, the carriage was raised, and the escorts had left the palace gate and mounted their horses, suddenly a call announced that Tuozhou had arrived—the escorts turned back inside and stood holding their tablets with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: One day the attendant ministers were escorting the emperor at Chonghua Palace. When the rites were finished and the imperial carriage was raised, the escorts had already left the palace gate and mounted their horses when a sudden summons announced Tuozhou's arrival. The escorts turned back inside and stood holding their tablets with great deference.

sentences.zh: 逢吉曰：「既出復入揖，臣子事君父之禮當如是耶？

translations.literal: Fengji said: "Having gone out and then coming back in to bow—is this how ministers should serve their sovereign and father?
translations.idiomatic: Fengji said, "You went out and then came back in to bow—is this how a minister serves his sovereign and father?"

sentences.zh: 」不揖而去。

translations.literal: Without bowing, he left.
translations.idiomatic: Without bowing himself, he walked away.

sentences.zh: 會部中會食，吏密報優人王喜除閤職，逢吉即言：「於上前效朱侍講進趨，以儒為戲者，豈可令汙閤職？

translations.literal: At a departmental meal together, a clerk secretly reported that the actor Wang Xi was being appointed to a Ge Office post. Fengji immediately said: "One who before the emperor mimicked Lecturer Zhu's hurried advance—who treats the Confucian as a jest—how can he be allowed to sully a Ge Office post?
translations.idiomatic: During a departmental meal, a clerk secretly reported that the actor Wang Xi was to be appointed to a Ge Office post. Fengji immediately said, "A man who before the emperor mimicked Lecturer Zhu's hurried advance and made a jest of the Confucian—how can he be allowed to defile a Ge Office post?"

sentences.zh: 」即抗疏力爭之。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial and argued strenuously against it.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial and argued against it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 同列密以告侂胄。

translations.literal: A colleague secretly informed Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague secretly told Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 時王喜之命實未出，遂以誣詆，出知太平州。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xi's appointment had in fact not yet been issued; Fengji was therefore accused of false slander and sent out as prefect of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi's appointment had in fact not yet been issued, so Fengji was accused of slander and sent out as prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He requested a sinecure and was appointed commissioner for the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure and was appointed commissioner for the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 起知贛州，已屬疾，卒，諡「獻簡」。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Ganzhou, but was already gravely ill; he died and was posthumously titled Xianjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Ganzhou, but was already gravely ill. He died and was given the posthumous title Xianjian.

sentences.zh: 弟逢年、逢辰，皆有文學行義，時稱「孫氏三龍」。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Fengnian and Fengchen were both men of literary talent and moral conduct; people of the time called them "the Three Dragons of the Sun clan."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Fengnian and Fengchen were both men of literary talent and moral conduct; people of the time called them "the Three Dragons of the Sun clan."

sentences.zh: 章穎，字茂獻，臨江軍人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, style Maoxian, was a native of Linjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, styled Maoxian, was a native of Linjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以兼經中鄉薦。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination having mastered multiple classics.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination by excelling in multiple classics.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣服，下詔求言，穎為萬言書附驛以聞，禮部奏名第一，孝宗稱其文似陸贄。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he issued an edict seeking advice. Ying composed a ten-thousand-character memorial and sent it by post relay to inform the throne. The Ministry of Rites reported his name first; Xiaozong said his writing resembled Lu Zhi's.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he issued an edict calling for counsel. Ying wrote a ten-thousand-character memorial and sent it by courier to the throne. The Ministry of Rites ranked him first on the list; Xiaozong said his prose recalled Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 調道州教授，作周敦頤祠。

translations.literal: He was assigned as professor at Daozhou and built a shrine to Zhou Dunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as professor at Daozhou and erected a shrine to Zhou Dunyi.

sentences.zh: 會宜章寇為亂，郡僚相繼引去，穎獨留。

translations.literal: When bandits at Yizhang rose in revolt, prefectural staff successively withdrew; Ying alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits at Yizhang rose in revolt, the prefectural staff withdrew one after another; Ying alone stayed.

sentences.zh: 寇平，郡守以功入為郎，奏穎有協贊之功，可大用。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, the prefect entered the capital as a court official for his merit and memorialized that Ying had assisted in the effort and could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits were suppressed, the prefect was promoted to court for his merit and memorialized that Ying had helped coordinate the effort and was fit for greater use.

sentences.zh: 乃召對，除太學錄。

translations.literal: He was summoned for an audience and appointed Director of Records in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for an audience and appointed Director of Records at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 禮部正奏第一人，初任即召對者自穎始。

translations.literal: When the Chief Administrator of Rites reported the top examination candidate, the first person summoned for an audience upon initial appointment began with Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chief Administrator of Rites reported the top examination candidate, Ying was the first ever to be summoned for an audience upon taking up an initial appointment.

sentences.zh: 時樞密都承旨王抃以言者奉外祠。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Bian, Commissioner-in-Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was granted an outside sinecure due to censor criticism.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Bian, Commissioner-in-Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was granted an outside sinecure after censors attacked him.

sentences.zh: 穎復言其風金使過求，欲己任調護以為功。

translations.literal: Ying again spoke, saying he treated Jin envoys with excessive harshness in his demands, wishing to reserve for himself the role of mediator to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying spoke out again, saying Wang Bian had been overbearing toward Jin envoys in his demands, hoping to keep the mediating role for himself and claim the credit.

sentences.zh: 孝宗謂其言太訐，久之不遷。

translations.literal: Xiaozong said his words were too cutting; for a long time he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong said his words were too sharp; for a long time he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 及奏考試官，孝宗曰：「章穎可。

translations.literal: When reporting on examination officials, Xiaozong said: "Zhang Ying will do."
translations.idiomatic: When examination officials were being reported on, Xiaozong said, "Zhang Ying will do."

sentences.zh: 」乃知上猶記其讜論也。

translations.literal: Thus they knew the emperor still remembered his forthright opinions.
translations.idiomatic: From this they knew the emperor still remembered his candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服闋，添差通判贛州，除太常博士。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, when the mourning period ended he was specially appointed Adjunct Prefect of Ganzhou and appointed Erudite of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, when the mourning period ended he was specially appointed Adjunct Prefect of Ganzhou and then appointed Erudite of the Court of Sacrificial Worship.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞何澹聞繼母訃，引不逮事之文，穎定議解官，澹猶未決去，乞下侍從朝列集議。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief He Tan received news of his stepmother's death and cited a passage on not being obliged to serve. Ying fixed the ruling that he should resign his office. Tan still had not decided to leave and requested that attendant ministers and the court assembly be convened for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief He Tan received word of his stepmother's death and cited a passage exempting him from mourning obligations. Ying ruled that he must resign his office. Tan still hesitated to leave and asked that attendant ministers and the court assembly be convened to debate the matter jointly.

sentences.zh: 太學諸生攻之曰：「朝廷專設奉常，議禮之所由出也。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial Academy attacked him, saying: "The court specially maintains the Court of Sacrificial Worship—the place whence ritual deliberation proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial Academy attacked him, saying, "The court maintains the Court of Sacrificial Worship precisely so ritual deliberation may proceed from it.

sentences.zh: 今不從議禮所由出之地，反以議禮不公，而欲侍從朝列集議，豈將啟逢迎希合，而為苟留進身之計乎？

translations.literal: Now, rather than deferring to the place whence ritual deliberation proceeds, you take ritual deliberation to be unfair and wish the attendant ministers and court assembly to deliberate jointly—are you not trying to open the way for currying favor and compliance, making a plan of opportunistic retention for advancement?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, instead of deferring to the very office from which ritual deliberation should come, you declare the deliberation unfair and want attendant ministers and the whole court to debate it together—are you not opening the door to flattery and compliance, scheming to hold on to your post for advancement?"

sentences.zh: 」除左司諫，時左相留正去，右相葛邲當國，穎論邲不足任大事，凡二十餘疏。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Secretariat Remonstrator. At the time Left Chancellor Liu Zheng had departed and Right Chancellor Ge Bi held state affairs. Ying criticized Ge Bi as unfit for great matters—in all more than twenty memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Secretariat Remonstrator. Left Chancellor Liu Zheng had already left office and Right Chancellor Ge Bi was directing state affairs. Ying criticized Ge Bi as unfit for great affairs, submitting more than twenty memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 從官議欲超除穎，俾去言職，庶可兩留。

translations.literal: Attendant officials deliberated wishing to promote Ying by extraordinary appointment, removing him from remonstrating office so both might be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials discussed promoting Ying by extraordinary appointment and removing him from remonstrating office so that both men might be kept.

sentences.zh: 光宗曰：「是好諫官，何以遷之？

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong said: "He is a good remonstrator—why move him?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong said, "He is a good remonstrator—why transfer him?"

sentences.zh: 」邲始出。

translations.literal: Ge Bi only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Ge Bi leave office.

sentences.zh: 穎屢疏請上問安重華宮，悉焚其稿。

translations.literal: Ying repeatedly memorialized asking the emperor to visit Chonghua Palace in inquiry; he burned all drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Ying repeatedly memorialized asking the emperor to visit Chonghua Palace to inquire after the retired emperor, and burned every draft.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，除侍御史兼侍講，尋權兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong took the throne, he was appointed Attendant Censor and Concurrent Lecturer, and soon given acting appointment as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, Ying was appointed Attendant Censor and Concurrent Lecturer, and soon given acting appointment as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，穎侍經幃。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou wielded power; Ying attended the imperial lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou held power, and Ying attended the imperial lectures.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諫官有言及趙汝愚者，卿等謂何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Remonstrators have spoken concerning Zhao Ruyu—what do you all think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Remonstrators have spoken about Zhao Ruyu—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」同列謾無可否，穎奏言：「天地變遷，人情危疑，加以敵人嫚侮，國勢未安，未可容易進退大臣，願降詔宣諭汝愚，無聽其去。

translations.literal: Colleagues vaguely neither affirmed nor denied; Ying memorialized, saying: "Heaven and earth shift, human hearts are doubtful and unsettled, and to this is added the enemy's contempt and insult—the nation's position is not secure. One cannot lightly advance or dismiss great ministers. I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict to instruct Ruyu not to heed those urging him to leave."
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues evaded the question with vague noncommittal replies. Ying memorialized, saying, "Heaven and earth are in turmoil, hearts are anxious and unsettled, and the enemy adds contempt on top of it—the realm is not yet secure. Great ministers cannot be advanced or dismissed lightly. I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict telling Ruyu not to listen to those urging him to go."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 奏請待罪，與郡；

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to await punishment and be sent to a prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to await punishment and be sent out to a prefecture;

sentences.zh: 御史劾穎阿黨，罷。

translations.literal: censors impeached Ying for partisan attachment, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: censors impeached Ying for factional collusion, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太學生周端朝等六人伏闕，辨汝愚被誣，且謂章穎言發於忠，首遭斥逐。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy students Zhou Duanchao and six others prostrated themselves at the palace gate, arguing that Ruyu had been slandered and that Zhang Ying's words sprang from loyalty and that he was the first to suffer expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy students Zhou Duanchao and six others prostrated themselves at the palace gate, arguing that Ruyu had been slandered and that Zhang Ying had spoken from loyalty and been the first cast out.

sentences.zh: 端朝等皆被罪，自是黨論遂起矣。

translations.literal: Duanchao and the others were all punished; from this the factional controversy arose.
translations.idiomatic: Duanchao and the others were all punished; from this the factional strife began.

sentences.zh: 穎家居久之，起知衢州，侍御史林行可劾罷之。

translations.literal: Ying lived at home for a long time, then was raised to serve as prefect of Quzhou; Attendant Censor Lin Xingke impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying lived in retirement for a long time, then was recalled as prefect of Quzhou; Attendant Censor Lin Xingke impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 尋知贛州，御史王益祥復劾，寢其命，再祠，需次知建寧府。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Ganzhou; Censor Wang Yixiang again impeached him, and the appointment was shelved. He received a second sinecure and awaited his turn to serve as prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Ganzhou, but Censor Wang Yixiang impeached him again and the appointment was shelved. He received another sinecure and waited his turn to serve as prefect of Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，除集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, he was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Advancing Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, he was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Advancing Worthies.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部侍郎兼侍講，對延和殿，上歎曰：「卿為權臣沮抑甚久。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Lecturer. At audience in the Yanhe Hall, the emperor sighed and said: "You were suppressed by a power-holder for a very long time."
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Lecturer. At audience in the Yanhe Hall, the emperor sighed and said, "You were held down by a power-holder for far too long."

sentences.zh: 」穎乞修改《甲寅龍飛事跡》誣筆。

translations.literal: Ying requested revision of slanderous passages in the 《Record of the Jiayin Ascension》.
translations.idiomatic: Ying asked that slanderous passages in the 《Record of the Jiayin Ascension》 be revised.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎，尋遷禮部尚書，升侍讀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and soon promoted to Minister of Rites, and elevated to Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, soon promoted to Minister of Rites, and elevated to Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 詔穎以紹熙、慶元譙令憲《玉牒辨誣》，余端禮、趙彥逾《甲寅龍飛記》及趙汝愚當時所記事，考訂削誣，從實上之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ying to take Qiao Lingxian's Jade Register Refutation of Slander from the Shaoxi and Qingyuan eras, Yu Duanli and Zhao Yanyu's Record of the Jiayin Ascension, and records of affairs at the time concerning Zhao Ruyu, examine and edit away slander, and submit according to truth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ying to take Qiao Lingxian's 《Jade Register Refutation of Slander》 from the Shaoxi and Qingyuan eras, Yu Duanli and Zhao Yanyu's 《Record of the Jiayin Ascension》, and Zhao Ruyu's contemporary records, examine them, strike out slander, and submit a truthful account.

sentences.zh: 丐去，奉祠。

translations.literal: He requested leave and was granted a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and was granted a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 以嘉定十一年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiading he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jiading he died, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 穎操履端直，生平風節不為窮達所移。

translations.literal: Ying's conduct was upright; throughout his life his integrity was unmoved by adversity or success.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's conduct was upright; throughout his life his moral bearing was unchanged whether in hardship or prosperity.

sentences.zh: 雖仕多偃蹇，而清議與之。

translations.literal: Though his official career was mostly beset with setbacks, public opinion stood with him.
translations.idiomatic: Though his official career was mostly stalled, public opinion stood with him.

sentences.zh: 方黨論之興，朱熹遺以書，略曰：「世道反覆，已足流涕；

translations.literal: When factional controversy arose, Zhu Xi sent him a letter that read in part: "The times turn back and forth—this is already enough to draw tears;
translations.idiomatic: When factional strife arose, Zhu Xi sent him a letter that read in part, "The times turn back and forth—this alone is enough to bring one to tears;

sentences.zh: 而握其事者怒猶未已，未知終安所至極耶？

translations.literal: yet he who holds the affair still has not ceased his wrath—I do not know where it will end in the end?
translations.idiomatic: yet the man who holds the reins still has not spent his anger—who knows where it will end?

sentences.zh: 然宗社有靈，公論未泯，異日必有任是責者，非公吾誰望耶？

translations.literal: Yet the altars of state have spirit; public opinion is not extinguished. Someday there will surely be one who bears this responsibility—if not you, whom do I look to?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the altars of state have their spirits, and public opinion is not dead. Someday someone must bear this burden—if not you, whom can I look to?"

sentences.zh: 」贈光祿大夫，諡「文肅」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous title "Wensu."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 商飛卿

translations.literal: Shang Feiqing
translations.idiomatic: Shang Feiqing

sentences.zh: 商飛卿，字翬仲，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Shang Feiqing, styled Huizhong, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Feiqing, styled Huizhong, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，由太學登進士第，任無為軍教授，累官至工部郎官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi he passed the metropolitan examination from the Imperial Academy, served as professor at Wuwei Army, and through successive promotions reached Secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunxi era he passed the metropolitan examination from the Imperial Academy, served as professor at Wuwei Army, and rose through successive promotions to Secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄柄國，氣焰薰灼，飛卿既至，未嚐輒一造請，踰月即丐去，提舉福建路常平茶鹽事。

translations.literal: At the time Han Tuozhou held the government and his arrogance scorched all; after Feiqing arrived he never once went to pay a visit. After a month he requested leave and was appointed Commissioner of Regular Grain and Salt for Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Tuozhou held the government and his arrogance blazed over all; after Feiqing arrived he never once went to call on him. Within a month he requested leave and was appointed Commissioner of Regular Grain and Salt for Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，以言事迕侂胄，罷為奉常。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor; for memorializing on affairs in opposition to Tuozhou he was dismissed to the Court of Sacrificial Worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Investigating Censor, but for memorializing in opposition to Tuozhou he was dismissed to the Court of Sacrificial Worship.

sentences.zh: 請外，以秘閣修撰為荊湖南路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He requested an outside post and, as Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion, served as Transport Judge for Jinghu South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He requested an outside post and, as Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion, served as Transport Judge for Jinghu South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後改司農卿，總領江東、淮西軍馬錢糧。

translations.literal: Later he was changed to Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and given overall charge of military horses, funds, and grain for Jiang-East and Huai-West.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and given overall charge of military horses, funds, and grain for Jiang-East and Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 金陵故有帥、漕治所，合戎騎二帥、留鑰、內侍，號六司，宴飲饋遺，費動萬計。

translations.literal: Jinling originally had headquarters for the military commissioner and transport commissioner; combined with the two cavalry commanders, the stay-behind commissioner, and the inner attendant—it was called the Six Offices. Banquets, drinking, and gifts cost tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling originally had headquarters for the military commissioner and the transport commissioner; together with the two cavalry commanders, the stay-behind commissioner, and the inner attendant, they were called the Six Offices. Banquets, feasting, and gift-giving ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 飛卿以身率儉，節縮浮苛，糧餉時斂散，稍稍以裕聞。

translations.literal: Feiqing personally set an example of frugality, cutting wasteful excess; grain supplies were timely in collection and disbursement, and gradually he became known for surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Feiqing personally practiced frugality and cut wasteful excess. Grain supplies were collected and disbursed on schedule, and gradually his name became associated with surplus.

sentences.zh: 開禧中，就擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaixi era he was promoted on the spot to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaixi era he was promoted on the spot to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 侂胄將舉師，嘗問餉計豐約，飛卿以實告。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was about to raise an army and once asked whether provisions were ample or scant; Feiqing told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was about to mobilize the army and once asked whether provisions were ample or scarce; Feiqing told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 比調遣浩繁，不克支，屬有旨俾飛卿軍前傳宣撫勞，值金兵大至，幾不免，以憂卒。

translations.literal: When deployments grew vast and could not be sustained, there came an order for Feiqing to go before the army as imperial envoy to proclaim comfort and encouragement. Just as Jin forces arrived in great numbers he nearly could not escape; he died of grief and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: When deployments multiplied and could no longer be sustained, an order came for Feiqing to go before the army as imperial envoy to proclaim comfort and encouragement. Jin forces arrived in great numbers and he nearly did not escape; he died of grief and anxiety.

sentences.zh: 劉穎，字公實，衢州西安人。

translations.literal: Liu Ying, styled Gongshi, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ying, styled Gongshi, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年進士，調溧陽主簿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing he passed the examination and was assigned as chief clerk at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing he passed the examination and was assigned as chief clerk at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時張浚留守建康，金師初退，府索民租未入者，穎白浚言：「師旅之後，宜先撫摩，當盡蠲逋賦。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jun was stay-behind commissioner at Jiankang; Jin forces had just withdrawn, and the prefecture demanded unpaid rent from the people. Ying told Jun: "After armies have passed, one should first soothe the people—unpaid levies should all be remitted."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Jun was stay-behind commissioner at Jiankang. Jin forces had just withdrawn, and the prefecture was demanding unpaid rent from the people. Ying told Jun, "After armies have passed through, the people should be soothed first—all unpaid levies should be remitted."

sentences.zh: 」浚喜，即奏閣免，由是知之，遣其子栻與遊。

translations.literal: Jun was pleased and immediately memorialized for wholesale exemption; from this he came to know Ying and sent his son Shi to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was pleased and immediately memorialized for a wholesale exemption. From this he came to know Ying and sent his son Shi to keep company with him.

sentences.zh: 教授全州，改官知鉛山縣，以外艱去。

translations.literal: He served as professor at Quanzhou, changed appointment to magistrate of Qianshan County, and left on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor at Quanzhou, changed appointment to magistrate of Qianshan County, and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 再知常熟縣，簽判潭州。

translations.literal: He again served as magistrate of Changshu County and as signing judge of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as magistrate of Changshu County and as signing judge of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 王佐為帥，負其能，盛氣以臨僚吏，穎約以中道，多屈而改為。

translations.literal: Wang Zuo was military commissioner; relying on his ability he bullied subordinate officials with overbearing air. Ying restrained him by the middle way, and Zuo often yielded and changed course.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo was military commissioner. Confident in his ability, he bullied subordinate officials with overbearing airs. Ying held him to the middle way, and Zuo often yielded and changed course.

sentences.zh: 及陳峒反，所擒賊多穎計策，帥上其功，曰：「簽判宜居臣上。

translations.literal: When Chen Dong rebelled, most captured bandits were taken through Ying's stratagems. The commissioner reported his merit, saying: "The signing judge's rank should be above mine."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Dong rebelled, most of the bandits captured were taken through Ying's stratagems. The commissioner reported his merit, saying, "The signing judge's rank should be above mine."

sentences.zh: 」召監進奏院，進太常寺主簿，遷丞，兼兵部郎官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to supervise the Memorial Submission Office, advanced to Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Assistant Director, and concurrently served as Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to supervise the Memorial Submission Office, advanced to Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Assistant Director, and concurrently served as Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 提舉浙西常平茶鹽，還澱山湖，以泄吳松江一水，禁民侵築，毋使逼塞大流，民田賴之。

translations.literal: As Commissioner of Regular Grain and Salt for Western Zhejiang he returned to Lake Dianshan to drain the single waterway of Wusong River, forbidding the people from encroaching in construction lest the main flow be blocked—the people's fields benefited.
translations.idiomatic: As Commissioner of Regular Grain and Salt for Western Zhejiang he returned to Lake Dianshan to open the Wusong River's single channel, forbidding the people from encroaching with construction lest the main flow be blocked—the people's fields benefited.

sentences.zh: 就遷提刑，以洗冤澤物為任，間詣獄，察不應繫者縱遣之。

translations.literal: He was promoted on the spot to Intendant; he took cleansing wrongs and benefiting the people as his charge, sometimes visiting prisons and releasing those who should not be detained.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted on the spot to Intendant. He took clearing wrongs and benefiting the people as his charge, sometimes visiting prisons himself and releasing those who should not be held.

sentences.zh: 御史以介僻劾罷。

translations.literal: Censors impeached and dismissed him for being stiff and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him for being stiff and aloof and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 除江西運判。

translations.literal: He was appointed Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江州德化縣田逃徙太半，守乞蠲稅，不報。

translations.literal: In Dehua County, Jiangzhou, fields had half fled abandonment; the prefect requested remission of tax, but no response came.
translations.idiomatic: In Dehua County, Jiangzhou, more than half the fields had been abandoned; the prefect requested remission of tax, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 穎以見種之稅均於荒萊，民願耕者第減之，上供自若，而逃田盡復。

translations.literal: Ying distributed the tax on surviving plots evenly over abandoned wasteland; for peasants willing to cultivate he reduced the tax, upper tribute remained as before, and abandoned fields were all restored.
translations.idiomatic: Ying spread the tax on surviving plots evenly over abandoned wasteland; for peasants willing to cultivate he reduced the levy, upper tribute remained as before, and the abandoned fields were all restored.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣、淮東轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and Deputy Transport Commissioner of Huai-East.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and Deputy Transport Commissioner of Huai-East.

sentences.zh: 初，水敗楚州城，修補未竟，劉超欲移築，穎因接伴金國使，入對言：「國家何苦捐百萬緡為軍帥幸賞地邪？

translations.literal: Initially flood had broken the walls of Chuzhou city; repairs were not finished when Liu Chao wished to relocate and rebuild. Ying, because he was receiving Jin envoys, entered audience and said: "Why should the state throw away a million strings of cash as a place for the military commander's opportune reward?"
translations.idiomatic: Flood had first broken the walls of Chuzhou city; repairs were not yet finished when Liu Chao wished to relocate and rebuild. Ying, while receiving Jin envoys, entered audience and said, "Why should the state throw away a million strings of cash to give a military commander a windfall?"

sentences.zh: 」光宗從之。

translations.literal: Guangzong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 除戶部郎中、淮東總領。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Overall Commander of Huai-East.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Overall Commander of Huai-East.

sentences.zh: 務場以額鈔抵賞，陰耗餉計，二十年無知此弊者，穎究覈得之，以所賣數論賞而總餉增羨，遷司農少卿、淮西總領。

translations.literal: Service stations used quota notes to offset rewards, secretly depleting provisions—for twenty years no one knew this abuse. Ying investigated and discovered it, used quantity sold to determine rewards, and overall provisioning increased surplus. He was promoted to Vice Director of Agriculture and Overall Commander of Huai-West.
translations.idiomatic: Service stations used quota notes to offset rewards, secretly draining provisions—for twenty years no one had known of this abuse. Ying investigated and uncovered it, used quantities sold to determine rewards, and overall provisioning grew surplus. He was promoted to Vice Director of Agriculture and Overall Commander of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 前主計者請自為都釀，抱淨息而利贏餘，其後稍虧，反以大軍錢佐之，邀糴江、淮，回易如負販狀。

translations.literal: Previous chief accountants had requested to serve as their own brewmasters, holding net profits for surplus gain; afterward there was gradual loss and they used great army funds to supplement it, buying grain on Jiang and Huai and trading back and forth like peddlers.
translations.idiomatic: Previous chief accountants had asked to serve as their own brewmasters, keeping net profits for surplus gain; afterward losses mounted and they used great army funds to make up the shortfall, buying grain on the Jiang and Huai and trading back and forth like peddlers.

sentences.zh: 穎以為失王人之體，遂罷之。

translations.literal: Ying considered this a loss of the kingly manner and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying considered this unworthy of a royal commissioner and abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 內府宣限既迫，每移供軍錢以應歲輸。

translations.literal: When inner palace urgent demands pressed close, each time they diverted army funds to meet annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When urgent demands from the inner palace pressed close, army funds were diverted each time to meet the annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 穎蒐吏弊，汰冗員，分月綱解，自是不復那移。

translations.literal: Ying investigated clerical abuses, eliminated redundant staff, divided monthly quota deliveries—in this way diversion ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ying investigated clerical abuses, eliminated redundant staff, and divided deliveries into monthly quotas—in this way diversion ceased.

sentences.zh: 尋除直寶謨閣、江東運副、知平江府，皆未行。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Direct Compiler of the Baomo Pavilion, Deputy Transport Commissioner of Jiang-East, and Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture—all without taking up the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Direct Compiler of the Baomo Pavilion, Deputy Transport Commissioner of Jiang-East, and Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture—none of which he took up.

sentences.zh: 除宗正少卿，遷起居郎兼實錄院檢討官，權戶部侍郎，升同修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan, promoted to Palace Secretary and Concurrent Reviser at the Veritable Records Institute, given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Revenue, and elevated to Concurrent Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan, promoted to Palace Secretary and Concurrent Reviser at the Veritable Records Institute, given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Revenue, and elevated to Concurrent Compiler.

sentences.zh: 以疾丐祠，提舉興國宮。

translations.literal: On account of illness he requested a sinecure and was appointed Commissioner for Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On account of illness he requested a sinecure and was appointed Commissioner for Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 除集英殿修撰、知寧國府，改知紹興府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Advancing Worthies and Prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, then changed to Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Advancing Worthies and Prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, then transferred to Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知平江府，徑歸，提舉興國宮。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture, went straight home, and was appointed Commissioner for Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture, went straight home, and was appointed Commissioner for Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知泉州，升華文閣待制，請興國祠以歸。

translations.literal: He was raised to serve as Prefect of Quanzhou, promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Wenhua Pavilion, and requested return to the Xingguo sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Prefect of Quanzhou, promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Wenhua Pavilion, and requested return to the Xingguo sinecure.

sentences.zh: 興國祠滿，除敷文閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: When the Xingguo sinecure term ended he was appointed Awaiting Orders at the Fuwén Pavilion with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xingguo sinecure term ended he was appointed Awaiting Orders at the Fuwén Pavilion and retired.

sentences.zh: 嘉定改元，召赴行在，落致仕，除刑部侍郎，辭，進龍圖閣待制、知婺州。

translations.literal: When the Jiading era began he was summoned to the capital; retirement was revoked and he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice. He declined and was advanced to Awaiting Orders at the Longtu Pavilion and Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiading era began he was summoned to the capital; his retirement was revoked and he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice. He declined and was advanced to Awaiting Orders at the Longtu Pavilion and Prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 請老，以寶謨閣直學士致仕。

translations.literal: He requested old age and retired as Direct Academician of the Baomo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement on account of age and retired as Direct Academician of the Baomo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於家，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died at home, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died at home, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 在孝宗朝，人臣爭承意自獻。

translations.literal: In Xiaozong's reign ministers competed to conform to the emperor's wishes and offer themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaozong's reign ministers competed to read the emperor's wishes and offer themselves up.

sentences.zh: 穎奏：「今日之失在輕聽人言，昔之施為，今復棄置，大損盛德。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized: "Today's failing lies in lightly heeding men's words—what was done yesterday is today abandoned again, greatly harming august virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized, "Today's failing is that the court lightly heeds men's words—what was done yesterday is abandoned today, greatly harming the emperor's virtue."

sentences.zh: 」孝宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 光宗時，論人主難克而易流者四，曰：逸豫無節、賜予無度、儒臣易疏、近幸易昵。

translations.literal: In Guangzong's time he spoke of four things hard for a ruler to overcome yet easy to drift toward: unbounded indulgence in ease, unbounded largesse, easily estranging Confucian ministers, easily drawing close to intimate favorites.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzong's time he spoke of four things hard for a ruler to resist yet easy to drift toward: unbounded indulgence in ease, unbounded largesse, easily estranging Confucian ministers, and easily drawing close to intimate favorites.

sentences.zh: 寧宗時，學禁初起，黨論日興。

translations.literal: In Ningzong's time, as the learning prohibition first arose, factional controversy grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: In Ningzong's time, as the learning prohibition first arose, factional strife grew daily.

sentences.zh: 穎奏：「願陛下御之以道，容之以德，不然，元祐、崇、觀之事可鑒也。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized: "I wish Your Majesty to govern them by the Way and accommodate them with virtue—or else, the affairs of Yuan You, Chong, and Guan may serve as a mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized, "I wish Your Majesty to govern them by the Way and accommodate them with virtue—or else the affairs of Yuan You, Chong, and Guan may serve as a mirror."

sentences.zh: 」其言皆切中於時。

translations.literal: His words all hit the mark of the time.
translations.idiomatic: His words all struck home at the time.

sentences.zh: 自浙西請外，凡徙麾節十餘年，有以淹速玄訊之，穎笑曰：「吾所欲也。

translations.literal: From requesting an outside post in Western Zhejiang, through more than ten years of changing banners and seals, some used obscurity to divine his fortunes; Ying smiled and said: "It is what I wanted."
translations.idiomatic: From requesting an outside post in Western Zhejiang through more than ten years of changing banners and seals, some tried to read his fortunes in the pace of his career; Ying smiled and said, "It is what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 」其在從班日，韓侂胄舊與周旋無間，方居中用事，而穎謝絕之。

translations.literal: When he was in the inner court ranks, Han Tuozhou had formerly associated with him without gap; just as he held central power, Ying broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in the inner court ranks, Han Tuozhou had formerly associated with him without reserve; just as Tuozhou held central power, Ying broke off relations.

sentences.zh: 常言：「士以不辱身為重。

translations.literal: He often said: "For a gentleman, not disgracing oneself is weightiest."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "For a gentleman, not disgracing oneself is what matters most."

sentences.zh: 」其為少宗正，而丞相趙汝愚適歸，相遇於廢寺，泥雨不能伸足，但僧床立語曰：「寄謝余參政，某雖去而人才猶在朝遷，幸善待之。

translations.literal: When he was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan, Chancellor Zhao Ruyu happened to be returning; they met at a ruined temple. Mud and rain prevented extending their feet—they could only stand beside a monk's bed and speak: "Please convey to Vice Administrator Yu—though I am gone, talented men remain; I hope you will treat them well in court promotions."
translations.idiomatic: When he was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan, Chancellor Zhao Ruyu happened to be returning home; they met at a ruined temple. Mud and rain kept them from stepping forward—they could only stand beside a monk's bed and speak: "Please tell Vice Administrator Yu: though I am gone, talented men remain at court; I hope you will treat them well in promotions."

sentences.zh: 」穎曰：「相公人才即參政人才也，使果賢，參政之責，非宰相之憂也。

translations.literal: Ying said: "Your Excellency's talent is the Vice Administrator's talent. If they are truly worthy, nurturing them is the Vice Administrator's responsibility—not the Chancellor's worry."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "Your Excellency's talent is the Vice Administrator's talent. If they are truly worthy, nurturing them is the Vice Administrator's duty—not the Chancellor's concern."

sentences.zh: 」余參政，端禮也。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Yu was Duanli.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Yu was Duanli.

sentences.zh: 余繼相，卒於善類多所全佑，穎之助云。

translations.literal: When Yu succeeded to the chancellorship he ultimately preserved many good men in several instances—Ying's assistance was part of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu succeeded to the chancellorship he ultimately preserved many good men in several instances—Ying's assistance was part of this.

sentences.zh: 徐邦憲

translations.literal: Xu Bangxian
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bangxian

sentences.zh: 徐邦憲，字文子，婺州義烏人。

translations.literal: Xu Bangxian, styled Wenzi, was a native of Yiwu in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bangxian, styled Wenzi, was a native of Yiwu in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，從陳傅良究名物義理，以通史傳百家之書。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick and penetrating; he studied with Chen Fuliang name-and-object principles and reason, to master the books of histories, classics, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and penetrating. He studied with Chen Fuliang the principles of names and things and moral reason, to master histories, classics, and the books of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，試禮部，第一人登進士第。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he tested at the Ministry of Rites, ranked first, and passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he tested at the Ministry of Rites, ranked first, and passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 三遷為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Through three promotions he became Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Through three promotions he became Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄開兵端，同惡附和，無敢先發一語議其非者，邦憲獨首言之。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou opened military hostilities; evil companions echoed him and none dared first to speak a word against it. Bangxian alone spoke first.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou opened military hostilities; his allies echoed him and none dared speak against it first. Bangxian alone spoke first.

sentences.zh: 丐外，知處州，陛辭，力諫用兵不可太驟。

translations.literal: He requested an outside post and was appointed Prefect of Chuzhou. At farewell audience he strongly remonstrated that military use could not be too hasty.
translations.idiomatic: He requested an outside post and was appointed Prefect of Chuzhou. At his farewell audience he strongly remonstrated that war could not be launched too hastily.

sentences.zh: 再歲召還，言：「求名義以息兵，莫若因建儲而肆赦，借殊常之恩，為弭兵之名，因行赦宥，大霈德澤。

translations.literal: After two years he was recalled and said: "To seek a righteous name to stop war, nothing is better than taking advantage of establishing an heir to grant a broad amnesty—borrowing extraordinary grace as a name for stopping war, and along with the amnesty extending great virtuous favor.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled and said, "To seek a righteous name for stopping war, nothing is better than using the establishment of an heir to grant a broad amnesty—borrowing extraordinary grace as a name for stopping war, and along with the amnesty extending great virtuous favor.

sentences.zh: 東委宣諭，西委宣撫，洗弄兵之咎，省戍邊之師；

translations.literal: East delegate imperial envoys to proclaim, west delegate commissioners to pacify—wash away the blame of reckless soldiers and reduce border garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the east delegate imperial envoys to proclaim, in the west delegate commissioners to pacify—wash away the blame of reckless soldiers and reduce border garrison troops;

sentences.zh: 發倉粟以賑餓殍，及農時而復民業。

translations.literal: release granary grain to relieve the starving dead, and restore the people's livelihood at farming season.
translations.idiomatic: release granary grain to relieve the starving dead, and restore the people's livelihood when farming season returns.

sentences.zh: 如此則建儲之義，正與息兵相為表裏也。」

translations.literal: In this way the meaning of establishing an heir aligns inside and out with stopping war."
translations.idiomatic: In this way the meaning of establishing an heir aligns inside and out with stopping war."

sentences.zh: 又上侂胄書，侂胄惡其言，嗾御史徐柟擊之，鐫秩罷祠。

translations.literal: He also submitted a letter to Tuozhou; Tuozhou hated his words and instigated Censor Xu Kan to attack him—reduction in rank, dismissal to sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a letter to Tuozhou. Tuozhou hated his words and instigated Censor Xu Kan to attack him—reduction in rank and dismissal to a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 未幾復官，除江西憲，改江東漕，以戶部郎為淮西總領。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored; appointed Intendant of Jiangxi, changed to Transport Commissioner of Jiang-East, and served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue as Overall Commander of Huai-West.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office; appointed Intendant of Jiangxi, changed to Transport Commissioner of Jiang-East, and served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Overall Commander of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 侂胄已誅，尚書倪思舉邦憲自代。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was already executed, Minister Ni Si recommended Bangxian to succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou had been executed, Minister Ni Si recommended Bangxian to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 召對，上言：「今日更化，未可與紹興乙亥同論。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience he said: "Today's renewal cannot be discussed on the same terms as Shaoxing yihai.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience he said, "Today's renewal cannot be discussed on the same terms as Shaoxing yihai.

sentences.zh: 秦檜專權，天下猶可以緝理，今侂胄專權，天下敗壞盡矣。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui monopolized power the realm could still be put in order; now Tuozhou monopolized power and the realm is ruined entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui monopolized power the realm could still be put in order; now that Tuozhou monopolized power the realm is ruined entirely.

sentences.zh: 」除尚右郎兼太子侍講，除左司，為金賀正使接伴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Section Gentleman and Concurrent Lecturer to the Crown Prince, appointed Left Secretariat, and served as receiving commissioner for Jin envoys coming to congratulate the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Section Gentleman and Concurrent Lecturer to the Crown Prince, appointed Left Secretariat, and served as receiving commissioner for Jin envoys coming to congratulate the New Year.

sentences.zh: 除宗正少卿，回權工部侍郎、知臨安府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan; on return he was given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works and Prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Clan; on his return he was given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works and Prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，知江州，奏乞郡，得節制屯戍兵，至郡疾，以寶謨閣待制致仕，卒於官，年五十七，諡「文肅」。

translations.literal: He requested a sinecure, was appointed Prefect of Jiangzhou, memorialized requesting the prefecture and received control of garrison troops. Upon reaching the prefecture he fell ill, retired as Awaiting Orders at the Baomo Pavilion, and died in office, aged fifty-seven; posthumous title "Wensu."
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure and was appointed Prefect of Jiangzhou. He memorialized requesting the prefecture and received control of garrison troops. Upon reaching the prefecture he fell ill, retired as Awaiting Orders at the Baomo Pavilion, and died in office, aged fifty-seven; posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：汪若海、柳約仕於南渡播遷之時，其志將以尊君父，故讀其《麟書》而悲之。

translations.literal: In the appraisal it is said: Wang Ruohai and Liu Yue served in the time when the south crossed in flight and displacement—their intent was to honor sovereign and father; therefore reading their 《Book of Lin》 moves one to grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the appraisal it is said: Wang Ruohai and Liu Yue served when the court fled south in displacement—their intent was to honor sovereign and father; therefore reading their 《Book of Lin》 moves one to grief.

sentences.zh: 張運、李舜臣職舉事修，遺愛在民。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun and Li Shunchen in office raised affairs well, and their lingering favor remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun and Li Shunchen in office raised affairs well, and their lingering kindness remains among the people.

sentences.zh: 孫逢吉、章穎辨正人之非邪，正學之非偽，君子哉！

translations.literal: Sun Fengji and Zhang Ying distinguished the wrong of upright men from the wrong of heterodoxy, genuine learning from counterfeit—true gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengji and Zhang Ying distinguished the wrong done to upright men from the wrong done to heterodoxy, genuine learning from counterfeit—true gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 商飛卿、劉穎、徐邦憲皆有立於權臣柄國之日，卓乎不為勢利所移，故能爾耶！

translations.literal: Shang Feiqing, Liu Ying, and Xu Bangxian all took their stand in the days when power-holders held the government—towering, unmoved by power and profit. For this reason they could be so!
translations.idiomatic: Shang Feiqing, Liu Ying, and Xu Bangxian all took their stand in the days when power-holders held the government—towering, unmoved by power and profit. That is why they could be so!
